name: Revelation
subtitle: An Apocalypse Made of Scripture
howToRead: Revelation never once says “as it is written” — it contains not a single formal quotation. Yet no book in the New Testament is more saturated with the Old: every vision is assembled from Daniel, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Exodus, Zechariah, and the Psalms. The chips beside each passage name the Scripture beneath it — almost all dashed (allusion), dotted (echo), or ◇ (figural), because John quotes nothing and remembers everything. A lighter chip and a trailing ? mark an echo that is faint or contested.

pericopes.text: This is the Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show to his servants the things which must happen soon, which he sent and made known by his angel to his servant, John, who testified to God’s word, and of the testimony of Jesus Christ, about everything that he saw. Blessed is he who reads and those who hear the words of the prophecy, and keep the things that are written in it, for the time is at hand.

echoes.text: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these: as for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what shall happen.
echoes.note: The programmatic phrase 'the things which must happen' (ha dei genesthai) reworks Daniel's 'what must happen hereafter' (LXX Dan 2:28–29, ha dei genesthai). High verbal volume on the apocalyptic-disclosure formula; John shortens Daniel's 'in the latter days' to 'soon,' compressing Daniel's eschatology into imminence.

echoes.text: Because you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God has made known to the king what shall happen hereafter: and the dream is certain, and its interpretation sure.
echoes.note: Reinforces the Danielic 'made known what will happen hereafter' as the source of John's 'show to his servants.' Thematic coherence (God reveals the certain future) supports the link; verbal echo is secondary to Dan 2:28–29.

echoes.text: Surely the Lord Yahweh will do nothing, unless he reveals his secret to his servants the prophets.
echoes.note: The pairing of revealing 'his secret to his servants the prophets' coheres with John's 'show to his servants' through the prophet-mediator John. Faint, conceptual echo only; no distinctive shared vocabulary in WEB/LXX, hence low confidence and contested.

pericopes.text: John, to the seven assemblies that are in Asia: Grace to you and peace, from God, who is and who was and who is to come; and from the seven Spirits who are before his throne; and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To him who loves us, and washed us from our sins by his blood; and he made us to be a Kingdom, priests to his God and Father; to him be the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.

echoes.text: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and he said, “You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
echoes.note: 'Who is and who was and who is to come' expands the divine Name of Exod 3:14 (LXX ho ōn, 'the one who is') into a three-tense formula. High thematic coherence on the eternal self-existent God; John adds 'who was' and 'who is to come' to render the Tetragrammaton's timelessness, a known Targumic/Hellenistic-Jewish expansion.

echoes.text: and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.”
echoes.note: 'He made us to be a Kingdom, priests to his God' directly reapplies the Sinai covenant charter 'a kingdom of priests' to the church. Strong verbal volume; John follows a reading like 'kingdom and priests' (cf. LXX basileion hierateuma), democratizing Israel's vocation onto the redeemed.

echoes.text: I will also appoint him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
echoes.note: 'The firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth' fuses both halves of Ps 89:27 (LXX 88:28), the royal-messianic enthronement of David's heir. Two distinct phrases recur together (firstborn + highest/ruler of earth's kings), giving high verbal volume; Christ's resurrection becomes the 'firstborn' coronation.

echoes.text: Behold, I have given him for a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander to the peoples.
echoes.note: 'The faithful witness' coheres with Isaiah's messianic 'witness to the peoples.' Thematic and partial verbal overlap on the title 'witness'; less distinctive than the Ps 89 / Exod echoes, so medium and arguably secondary.

echoes.text: Then he answered and spoke to me, saying, “This is Yahweh’s word to Zerubbabel, saying, ‘Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit,’ says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: The 'seven Spirits before his throne' may draw on Zechariah's vision-cycle of the Spirit and the seven lamps/eyes (Zech 4:2, 10). Faint; the sevenfold Spirit more likely develops Isa 11:2's enumerated Spirit, so low confidence and contested.

pericopes.text: Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, including those who pierced him. All the tribes of the earth will mourn over him. Even so, Amen. “I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, “who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty.”

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: 'He is coming with the clouds' lifts Daniel's 'one like a son of man' coming 'with the clouds of the sky.' Very high verbal volume and recurrence (this is Revelation's signature christophany text); John applies Daniel's heavenward enthronement to Christ's parousia toward earth.

echoes.text: I will pour on the house of David, and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplication; and they will look to me whom they have pierced; and they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for his only son, and will grieve bitterly for him, as one grieves for his firstborn.
echoes.note: 'Those who pierced him' and 'all the tribes will mourn' weave together Zech 12:10's piercing and mourning. High verbal volume; John follows the Hebrew 'whom they pierced' (the LXX reads 'because they mocked/danced'), agreeing with John 19:37 against the LXX — a noted Hebrew-vs-LXX divergence.

echoes.text: The land will mourn, every family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart;
echoes.note: 'All the tribes of the earth will mourn over him' extends Zech 12:12's catalog of mourning families. Reinforces the Zechariah piercing-and-mourning complex; John universalizes Zechariah's tribes of the land into 'all the tribes of the earth.'

echoes.text: This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.
echoes.note: 'I am the Alpha and the Omega' is a Greek-alphabet equivalent of Isaiah's divine self-predication 'I am the first and the last.' High thematic coherence with the Deutero-Isaianic monotheism formula; John recasts the merism into the first and last Greek letters, claiming exhaustive divine sovereignty.

echoes.text: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and he said, “You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
echoes.note: The repeated 'who is and who was and who is to come' restates the Exod 3:14 Name (LXX ho ōn). Recurrence from 1:4 raises verbal volume; here joined to 'the Almighty' (LXX pantokratōr), the standard rendering of 'Yahweh of Armies / El Shaddai.'

pericopes.text: I John, your brother and partner with you in oppression, Kingdom, and perseverance in Christ Jesus, was on the isle that is called Patmos because of God’s Word and the testimony of Jesus Christ. I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, and I heard behind me a loud voice, like a trumpet saying, “What you see, write in a book and send to the seven assemblies: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.”

echoes.text: On the third day, when it was morning, there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet; and all the people who were in the camp trembled.
echoes.note: The 'loud voice, like a trumpet' evokes the Sinai theophany, where God's voice attends 'an exceedingly loud trumpet.' Strong thematic coherence (divine self-revelation announced by trumpet); John casts Patmos as a new Sinai where the prophet receives the word.

echoes.text: When I looked, behold, a hand was stretched out to me; and, behold, a scroll of a book was therein; He spread it before me: and it was written within and without; and there were written therein lamentations, and mourning, and woe. He said to me, Son of man, eat that which you find. Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel.
echoes.note: The command 'What you see, write in a book and send' replays Ezekiel's call to receive a written scroll and deliver it to God's people. High coherence within the prophetic-commission genre that structures Rev 1; John substitutes 'write/send' for Ezekiel's 'eat/speak.'

echoes.text: Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of Yahweh comes, for it is close at hand:
echoes.note: The trumpet-voice may also carry Joel's eschatological alarm announcing the Day of Yahweh, consonant with 'the Lord's day' just named. Verbal volume is modest (shared image, not phrasing), so medium and contested against the Sinai/Exod 19 reading.

echoes.text: But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run back and forth, and knowledge shall be increased.”
echoes.note: The instruction to commit the vision 'to a book' inverts Daniel's command to 'seal the book,' part of Revelation's deliberate contrast (the time being 'at hand,' 1:3, so the book is opened not sealed). Faint, structural echo only.

pericopes.text: I turned to see the voice that spoke with me. Having turned, I saw seven golden lamp stands. And among the lamp stands was one like a son of man, clothed with a robe reaching down to his feet, and with a golden sash around his chest. His head and his hair were white as white wool, like snow. His eyes were like a flame of fire. His feet were like burnished brass, as if it had been refined in a furnace. His voice was like the voice of many waters. He had seven stars in his right hand. Out of his mouth proceeded a sharp two-edged sword. His face was like the sun shining at its brightest.

echoes.text: I lifted up my eyes, and looked, and behold, a man clothed in linen, whose thighs were adorned with pure gold of Uphaz: his body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches, and his arms and his feet like burnished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
echoes.note: The whole figure — robe, golden belt, eyes like fire, feet like burnished brass, resounding voice — is built on Daniel's glorious man. Very high verbal volume across multiple clustered details; this is the dominant template for the inaugural christophany.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: 'One like a son of man' is verbatim from Dan 7:13. High recurrence (cf. 1:7); John strikingly transfers to this 'son of man' the white-wool hair that Daniel gives the Ancient of Days, identifying Christ with God.

echoes.text: I saw until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
echoes.note: 'His head and his hair were white as white wool, like snow' reproduces Dan 7:9's description of the Ancient of Days. High verbal volume on the doubled simile (wool + snow); the deliberate transfer from the Ancient of Days to the son of man is a high-coherence Christological move.

echoes.text: Behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like the sound of many waters; and the earth shined with his glory.
echoes.note: 'His voice was like the voice of many waters' matches Ezek 43:2 nearly verbatim (LXX phōnē hydatōn pollōn). High verbal volume; the divine-glory association in Ezekiel transfers the theophanic voice directly to the risen Christ.

echoes.text: When they went, I heard the noise of their wings like the noise of great waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a noise of tumult like the noise of an army: when they stood, they let down their wings.
echoes.note: Ezek 1:24 supplies the same 'voice/noise of many waters' simile, here joined to 'the voice of the Almighty,' reinforcing the theophanic register. Slightly less close in wording than Ezek 43:2, so medium and arguably the secondary Ezekiel source.

echoes.text: and he has made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand, he has hidden me: and he has made me a polished shaft; in his quiver has he kept me close:
echoes.note: 'Out of his mouth proceeded a sharp two-edged sword' draws on the Servant's 'mouth like a sharp sword.' Strong thematic coherence (the word that judges proceeds from the mouth); John intensifies to a 'two-edged' sword, blending Isa 49:2 with Isa 11:4.

echoes.text: but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.
echoes.note: The sword/word 'out of his mouth' that judges fuses Isa 11:4's messianic 'rod of his mouth' with Isa 49:2. High thematic coherence on the judging messianic word; the two Isaiah texts together yield Revelation's recurring mouth-sword motif.

echoes.text: He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I have seen, and behold, a lamp stand all of gold, with its bowl on the top of it, and its seven lamps on it; there are seven pipes to each of the lamps, which are on the top of it;
echoes.note: The 'seven golden lamp stands' develop Zechariah's single golden lampstand with seven lamps. Real verbal overlap (golden lampstand, sevenfold light), but John multiplies the one menorah into seven (the churches), a deliberate transformation, so medium.

echoes.text: These are the garments which they shall make: a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a coat of checker work, a turban, and a sash: and they shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, and his sons, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.
echoes.note: The full-length robe and golden sash recall the high-priestly vestments (LXX podērēs, the very word used in Rev 1:13). Verbal volume rests on the rare term podērēs shared with Exod 28:4/29:5 LXX, presenting Christ as priest among the lampstands; medium because the figure is primarily Danielic.

echoes.text: “So let all your enemies perish, Yahweh, but let those who love him be as the sun when it rises in its strength.” Then the land had rest forty years.
echoes.note: 'His face was like the sun shining at its brightest' may echo the 'sun rising in its strength' of Deborah's song (and cf. Mal 4:2, the sun of righteousness). Faint, image-level echo with no distinctive shared phrasing, hence low and contested.

pericopes.text: When I saw him, I fell at his feet like a dead man. He laid his right hand on me, saying, “Don’t be afraid. I am the first and the last, and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever more. Amen. I have the keys of Death and of Hades. Write therefore the things which you have seen, and the things which are, and the things which will happen hereafter; the mystery of the seven stars which you saw in my right hand, and the seven golden lamp stands. The seven stars are the angelsof the seven assemblies. The seven lamp stands are seven assemblies.

echoes.text: So he came near where I stood; and when he came, I was frightened, and fell on my face: but he said to me, Understand, son of man; for the vision belongs to the time of the end. Now as he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face toward the ground; but he touched me, and set me upright.
echoes.note: The seer 'falling' overwhelmed and then being 'touched/raised' with the reassurance not to fear follows Daniel's recurring vision-reaction pattern (also Dan 10:9–10, 12). High coherence within the apocalyptic-call form; Christ takes the angel's reviving role.

echoes.text: This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.
echoes.note: 'I am the first and the last' is verbatim divine self-predication from Isaiah. High verbal volume and recurrence (cf. Alpha/Omega, 1:8); the risen Christ assumes a formula Isaiah reserves for Yahweh alone, an unambiguous high-Christology claim.

echoes.text: “Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.
echoes.note: Reinforces 'the first and the last' from a second Deutero-Isaiah occurrence, strengthening the recurrence criterion. High coherence; the doubled Isaianic witness shows John is citing a fixed monotheistic title, not an isolated phrase.

echoes.text: Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, Yahweh, the first, and with the last, I am he.”
echoes.note: A third Isaianic 'I, the first... and the last' that also pairs with 'I am he,' echoed in Christ's 'I am the Living one.' Medium because slightly less verbally exact than Isa 44:6/48:12, but it deepens the recurrence pattern.

echoes.text: I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder. He will open, and no one will shut. He will shut, and no one will open.
echoes.note: 'I have the keys of Death and of Hades' draws on Isaiah's image of the authoritative 'key' that opens and shuts (explicitly reused at Rev 3:7). High thematic coherence on delegated sovereign authority; John transfers the key from Eliakim's stewardship to Christ's power over the realm of the dead.

echoes.text: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these: as for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what shall happen.
echoes.note: 'The things which will happen hereafter' (and 'mystery,' mystērion) restates the Danielic disclosure formula from 1:1, framing the book. High recurrence; 'mystery of the seven stars' uses Daniel's revelation-of-secrets vocabulary (LXX mystērion, Dan 2:28–29).

echoes.text: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol. I will redeem them from death! Death, where are your plagues? Sheol, where is your destruction? “Compassion will be hidden from my eyes.
echoes.note: Christ holding 'the keys of Death and of Hades' coheres with Yahweh's claim to ransom from the power of Sheol/Death and to command Death and Hades. Thematic, not verbal; supports the keys-over-death motif but is the secondary source to Isa 22:22.

echoes.text: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
echoes.note: The 'gates of death' over which only God has knowledge/authority faintly underlies Christ's possession of the 'keys of Death.' Image-level echo with no shared distinctive wording, so low and contested.

pericopes.text: “To the angel of the assembly in Ephesus write: “He who holds the seven stars in his right hand, he who walks among the seven golden lamp stands says these things: “I know your works, and your toil and perseverance, and that you can’t tolerate evil men, and have tested those who call themselves apostles, and they are not, and found them false. You have perseverance and have endured for my name’s sake, and have not grown weary. But I have this against you, that you left your first love. Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and repent and do the first works; or else I am coming to you swiftly, and will move your lamp stand out of its place, unless you repent. But this you have, that you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate. He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the Paradise of my God.

echoes.text: Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
echoes.note: The overcomer's reward of eating "from the tree of life" reverses the Edenic loss. Strong on Hays' volume (the phrase עץ החיים / ξύλον τῆς ζωῆς is verbatim) and recurrence (the motif frames the whole Apocalypse, recurring at Rev 22:2,14). LXX and MT agree on the phrase.

echoes.text: Yahweh God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...” Therefore Yahweh God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken. So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim/f + cherubim are powerful angelic creatures, messengers of God with wings. See Ezekiel 10./f* at the east of the garden of […]
echoes.note: Typological reversal: access to the tree of life, barred by cherubim and the flaming sword after the expulsion, is now restored to the conqueror. High on thematic coherence and satisfaction — Revelation reads the Christ-event as undoing the Fall. "Paradise" (παράδεισος) is the LXX rendering of the garden of Eden, a clear LXX-mediated lexical link.

echoes.text: The cedars in the garden of God could not hide it; the fir trees were not like its boughs, and the plane trees were not as its branches; nor was any tree in the garden of God like it in its beauty. I made it beautiful by the multitude of its branches, so that all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied it.
echoes.note: Faint lexical support for the unusual phrase "Paradise of my God" (τῷ παραδείσῳ τοῦ θεοῦ μου); Ezek 28:13 and 31:8-9 supply "Eden, the garden of God." Low confidence; the Genesis tradition is the primary source. Flagged contested as background rather than direct echo.

pericopes.text: “To the angel of the assembly in Smyrna write: “The first and the last, who was dead, and has come to life says these things: “I know your works, oppression, and your poverty (but you are rich), and the blasphemy of those who say they are Jews, and they are not, but are a synagogue of Satan. Don’t be afraid of the things which you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, that you may be tested; and you will have oppression for ten days. Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life. He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. He who overcomes won’t be harmed by the second death.

echoes.text: This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.
echoes.note: The self-designation "the first and the last" applies a divine title of Yahweh (Isa 41:4; 44:6; 48:12) to the risen Christ. High on volume (verbatim πρῶτος καὶ ἔσχατος) and theological emphasis. LXX and MT agree.

echoes.text: Test your servants, I beg you, ten days; and let them give us vegetables to eat, and water to drink. Then let our faces be looked on before you, and the face of the youths who eat of the king’s dainties; and as you see, deal with your servants. So he listened to them in this matter, and proved them ten days.
echoes.note: The "ten days" of tribulation may echo the ten-day testing of Daniel and his companions, a stylized period of trial that ends in vindication. Low confidence; "ten days" is also simply a short delimited period. Flagged contested.

echoes.text: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
echoes.note: The promise that the conqueror "won't be harmed by the second death" presupposes a resurrection-of-the-just / judgment scheme rooted in Dan 12:2. "Crown of life" is faint (no clear OT antecedent; possibly the victor's wreath / Wisdom-tradition crown imagery). Low confidence.

pericopes.text: “To the angel of the assembly in Pergamum write: “He who has the sharp two-edged sword says these things: “I know your works and where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is. You hold firmly to my name, and didn’t deny my faith in the days of Antipas my witness, my faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells. But I have a few things against you, because you have there some who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to throw a stumbling block before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols, and to commit sexual immorality. So you also have some who hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans likewise. Repent therefore, or else I am coming to you quickly, and I will make war against them with the sword of my mouth. He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes, to him I will give of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written, which no one knows but he who receives it.

echoes.text: Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Yahweh in the matter of Peor, and so the plague was among the congregation of Yahweh.
echoes.note: The Balaam tradition — that Balaam "taught Balak" to entice Israel into idolatry and immorality — derives from the harmonized reading of Num 31:16 with Num 25. High on coherence: Revelation depends on this interpretive tradition (not just the Numbers narrative, where Balaam blesses Israel), making Balaam a cipher for false teachers. LXX/MT agree.

echoes.text: Israel stayed in Shittim; and the people began to play the prostitute with the daughters of Moab; for they called the people to the sacrifices of their gods. The people ate and bowed down to their gods.
echoes.note: The twin charge — "to eat things sacrificed to idols, and to commit sexual immorality" — maps directly onto the Baal-Peor episode (eating sacrifices to other gods + harlotry with the Moabite women). High volume and historical coherence. The pairing φαγεῖν εἰδωλόθυτα / πορνεῦσαι reflects this narrative.

echoes.text: The children of Israel traveled, and encamped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho. Balak the son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites. Moab was very afraid of the people, because they were many. Moab was distressed because of the children of Israel. Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this multitude will lick up all that is around us, as the ox licks up the grass of the field.” Balak the son of Zippor was king of Moab […]
echoes.note: Supplies the named figures "Balaam" and "Balak" and the master-pupil relationship Revelation assumes ("who taught Balak"). The figural reading — Balaam as archetypal corrupter of God's people for gain — is developed in Second Temple tradition and shared with 2 Peter 2:15 and Jude 11. High.

echoes.text: Moses said to Aaron, “Take a pot, and put an omer-full of manna in it, and lay it up before Yahweh, to be kept throughout your generations.” As Yahweh commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.
echoes.note: "Hidden manna" (τοῦ μάννα τοῦ κεκρυμμένου) draws on the jar of manna laid up "before the Testimony" in the ark. The adjective "hidden" reflects the later tradition (2 Macc 2:4-8) that Jeremiah concealed the ark and its manna, to be revealed at the eschaton — a strong coherence link to the messianic-banquet expectation. High.

echoes.text: and he has made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand, he has hidden me: and he has made me a polished shaft; in his quiver has he kept me close:
echoes.note: The Christ-speaker's "sharp two-edged sword" and "the sword of my mouth" echo the Servant whose mouth is "like a sharp sword." Medium-high on volume; the word-as-weapon image is distinctive. Combines with Isa 11:4. LXX μάχαιραν ὀξεῖαν aligns with Rev ρομφαίαν ἀμφίστομον ὀξεῖαν.

echoes.text: but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.
echoes.note: The messianic "rod of his mouth" / "breath of his lips" that slays the wicked underwrites "I will make war against them with the sword of my mouth." Medium confidence; reinforces the Davidic-judge typology. The LXX (πατάξει γῆν τῷ λόγῳ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ) sharpens the speech-as-sword motif.

echoes.text: The nations shall see your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of Yahweh shall name.
echoes.note: "A new name written, which no one knows but he who receives it" echoes the eschatological "new name" given by Yahweh to redeemed Zion (cf. also Isa 65:15). Medium confidence on the lexical phrase ὄνομα καινόν; the secrecy element is Revelation's own development.

echoes.text: [source text not in the World English Bible]
echoes.note: The "white stone" (ψῆφον λευκήν) has no single OT antecedent; proposed backgrounds include the Urim/priestly stones, an acquittal token, or an amulet bearing a secret name. The hidden-manna-restored motif is paralleled in 2 Baruch 29:8. Low confidence; included for maximal inventory.

pericopes.text: “To the angel of the assembly in Thyatira write: “The Son of God, who has his eyes like a flame of fire, and his feet are like burnished brass, says these things: “I know your works, your love, faith, service, patient endurance, and that your last works are more than the first. But I have this against you, that you tolerate yourwoman, Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess. She teaches and seduces my servants to commit sexual immorality, and to eat things sacrificed to idols. I gave her time to repent, but she refuses to repent of her sexual immorality. Behold, I will throw her into a bed, and those who commit adultery with her into great oppression, unless they repent of her works. I will kill her children with Death, and all the assemblies will know that I am he who searches the minds and hearts. I will give to each one of you according to your deeds. But to you I say, to the rest who are in Thyatira, as many as don’t have this teaching, who don’t know what some call ‘the deep things of Satan,’ to you I say, I am not putting any other burden on you. Nevertheless, hold that which you have firmly until I come. He who overcomes, and he who keeps my works to the end, to him I will give authority over the nations. He will rule them with a rod of iron, shattering them like clay pots;as I also have received of my Father: and I will give him the morning star. He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.

echoes.text: Ask of me, and I will give the nations for your inheritance, the uttermost parts of the earth for your possession. You shall break them with a rod of iron. You shall dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.”
echoes.note: The closest Revelation comes to formal citation: "I will give him authority over the nations. He will rule them with a rod of iron, shattering them like clay pots" reproduces Ps 2:8-9 nearly verbatim. Highest volume in the chapter. Revelation follows the LXX ποιμανεῖς ("shepherd/rule") of תרעם ("break") in Ps 2:9 — a notable LXX-vs-MT divergence: MT reads "break them" (râʿâʿ), LXX "rule/shepherd them," and Revelation's ποιμανεῖ reflects the LXX vocalization.

echoes.text: I, Yahweh, search the mind, I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.
echoes.note: "I am he who searches the minds and hearts. I will give to each one of you according to your deeds" fuses the divine self-predication of Jer 17:10 with its recompense clause. High on volume and structure: the two halves (searching reins/hearts + repaying according to deeds) appear together in both texts. ἐραυνῶν νεφροὺς καὶ καρδίας is LXX idiom.

echoes.text: I see him, but not now. I see him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob. A scepter will rise out of Israel, and shall strike through the corners of Moab, and break down all the sons of Sheth.
echoes.note: "I will give him the morning star" draws on Balaam's messianic "star out of Jacob" — a notable inclusio with the same chapter's Balaam-as-corrupter theme (2:14): Balaam both prophesies the true Star and (in tradition) corrupts Israel. High on coherence; reinforced by the wider star-Messiah expectation. Distinguish from the planet Venus / ἀστὴρ ὁ πρωϊνός imagery of Rev 22:16.

echoes.text: As if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, he took as wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshiped him.
echoes.note: "Jezebel" is a typological label for the Thyatiran false prophetess. The historical Jezebel introduced Baal worship and persecuted the prophets; Revelation reuses her as the archetype of seductive syncretism within the covenant community. High on coherence — the name is deployed symbolically, not biographically.

echoes.text: When Joram saw Jehu, he said, “Is it peace, Jehu?” He answered, “What peace, so long as the prostitution of your mother Jezebel and her witchcraft abound?”
echoes.note: Supplies the specific charge of Jezebel's "prostitution" (πορνεῖαι) and sorcery, which Revelation maps onto the Thyatiran teacher who "seduces my servants to commit sexual immorality." The judgment that her "children" are killed (2:23) further echoes the violent end of Jezebel's house in Jehu's purge (2 Kings 9-10). High.

echoes.text: his body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches, and his arms and his feet like burnished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
echoes.note: The opening self-description — "eyes like a flame of fire" and "feet like burnished brass" — is drawn from the angelophany of Dan 10:6 (eyes as flaming torches, arms and feet like burnished brass). High on volume; both distinctive images co-occur in source and target. The "burnished brass" (χαλκολιβάνῳ) wording is Revelation's coinage atop the LXX brass imagery.

echoes.text: Their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf’s foot; and they sparkled like burnished brass.
echoes.note: Secondary support for "feet like burnished brass": the living creatures of Ezekiel's throne vision sparkle "like burnished brass." Medium confidence; Dan 10:6 is the primary source, but the merkabah tradition reinforces the metal-feet image. LXX ἐξαστράπτων χαλκός.

echoes.text: Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end, but establish the righteous; their minds and hearts are searched by the righteous God.
echoes.note: A second witness to the "God who searches minds and hearts" formula behind 2:23, parallel to Jer 17:10 and Ps 139:1,23. Medium confidence; Jeremiah remains primary because it also supplies the recompense clause. ἐτάζων καρδίας καὶ νεφροὺς (LXX).

echoes.text: Israel stayed in Shittim; and the people began to play the prostitute with the daughters of Moab; for they called the people to the sacrifices of their gods. The people ate and bowed down to their gods.
echoes.note: The Thyatiran charge repeats the Pergamum/Baal-Peor pairing — "commit sexual immorality, and to eat things sacrificed to idols" — binding the two letters to the same Numbers 25 paradigm of idol-food plus harlotry. Medium confidence here (the Jezebel typology is primary), included to mark the recurring structural echo.

pericopes.text: “And to the angel of the assembly in Sardis write: “He who has the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars says these things: “I know your works, that you have a reputation of being alive, but you are dead. Wake up, and keep the things that remain, which you were about to throw away, for I have found no works of yours perfected before my God. Remember therefore how you have received and heard. Keep it, and repent. If therefore you won’t watch, I will come as a thief, and you won’t know what hour I will come upon you. Nevertheless you have a few names in Sardis that did not defile their garments. They will walk with me in white, for they are worthy. He who overcomes will be arrayed in white garments, and I will in no way blot his name out of the book of life, and I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels. He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.

echoes.text: Yet now, if you will, forgive their sin—and if not, please blot me out of your book which you have written.” Yahweh said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.
echoes.note: Blotting a name out of God's written book. Strong verbal+thematic correspondence (Hays: volume, recurrence) to 3:5 'blot his name out of the book of life.' Exodus has 'my book'/'your book'; Revelation adds 'of life' (βίβλος τῆς ζωῆς). LXX and Hebrew agree on the blotting idiom.

echoes.text: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, and not be written with the righteous.
echoes.note: The only OT verse with the exact phrase 'book of life' (LXX Ps 68:29 βίβλος ζώντων). Closest verbal source for Rev 3:5; high volume + thematic fit (registry of the righteous). Note LXX 'book of the living' vs MT 'book of life.'

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
echoes.note: Eschatological registry: deliverance of 'everyone who is found written in the book.' Revelation is saturated with Daniel; the heavenly book of the saved underlies the promise of 3:5. Hays: recurrence (Daniel pervades Rev) + thematic coherence.

echoes.text: I saw until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
echoes.note: White garments / clothing 'white as snow' for the heavenly/vindicated. Feeds the white-garment imagery of 3:4–5. Diffuse but recurrent Danielic palette in Revelation.

echoes.text: He answered and spoke to those who stood before him, saying, “Take the filthy garments off of him.” To him he said, “Behold, I have caused your iniquity to pass from you, and I will clothe you with rich clothing.”
echoes.note: Defiled (filthy) garments removed and replaced with clean/rich clothing = vindication. Background to 'did not defile their garments' and being 'arrayed in white.' Figural: garment = moral/cultic state.

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: Garments of salvation / robe of righteousness as eschatological clothing of the redeemed. Faint thematic resonance with white garments of the worthy; no distinctive verbal link.

pericopes.text: “To the angel of the assembly in Philadelphia write: “He who is holy, he who is true, he who has the key of David, he who opens and no one can shut, and who shuts and no one opens, says these things: “I know your works (behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one can shut), that you have a little power, and kept my word, and didn’t deny my name. Behold, I give of the synagogue of Satan, of those who say they are Jews, and they are not, but lie. Behold, I will make them to come and worship before your feet, and to know that I have loved you. Because you kept my command to endure, I also will keep you from the hour of testing, which is to come on the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth. I am coming quickly! Hold firmly that which you have, so that no one takes your crown. He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God, and he will go out from there no more. I will write on him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from my God, and my own new name. He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.

echoes.text: I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder. He will open, and no one will shut. He will shut, and no one will open.
echoes.note: The clearest near-quotation in the chapter: 'key of David... he opens and no one shuts, he shuts and no one opens' (Eliakim oracle) reapplied to Christ in 3:7. Very high volume + verbal correspondence. Rev follows the Hebrew/LXX sense closely; 'no one can shut' renders the same antithetic couplet.

echoes.text: The sons of those who afflicted you shall come bending to you; and all those who despised you shall bow themselves down at the soles of your feet; and they shall call you The city of Yahweh, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
echoes.note: Former oppressors 'come bowing' and bow at the soles of your feet — directly behind 3:9 'worship before your feet.' Strong thematic+verbal (feet, bowing of enemies of Zion). Reversal motif: nations honor the elect community.

echoes.text: Kings shall be your nursing fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers: they shall bow down to you with their faces to the earth, and lick the dust of your feet; and you shall know that I am Yahweh; and those who wait for me shall not be disappointed.”
echoes.note: Kings/nations 'bow down to you with their faces to the earth' and 'you will know that I am Yahweh' — paralleling 3:9 'worship before your feet, and to know that I have loved you.' The recognition-formula ('know that...') is a tight structural match.

echoes.text: Thus says Yahweh: “The labor of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia, and the Sabeans, men of stature, shall come over to you, and they shall be yours. They will go after you. They shall come over in chains; and they will bow down to you. They will make supplication to you: ‘Surely God is in you; and there is no one else. There is no other god.
echoes.note: Foreigners 'come over... bow down... make supplication: Surely God is in you.' Submission-of-the-nations-to-Zion topos underlying 3:9. Hays: recurrence (Rev clusters Isaianic Zion-pilgrimage texts).

echoes.text: The nations shall see your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of Yahweh shall name.
echoes.note: 'You will be called by a new name, which Yahweh's mouth will name' — source for 'my own new name' written on the overcomer (3:12). High verbal correspondence on the 'new name' motif.

echoes.text: You shall leave your name for a curse to my chosen; and the Lord Yahweh will kill you; and he will call his servants by another name:
echoes.note: 'He will call his servants by another name' — the new-name-for-the-elect (vs. old name as curse) behind 3:12. Pairs with Isa 62:2; thematic coherence with the eschatological renaming of God's servants.

echoes.text: It shall be eighteen thousand reeds around: and the name of the city from that day shall be, Yahweh is there.
echoes.note: The naming of the eschatological city ('Yahweh is there') is the structural model for 'the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem' (3:12). Ezekiel's temple-city vision (40–48) deeply shapes Rev's New Jerusalem; high recurrence + thematic fit.

echoes.text: to them I will give in my house and within my walls a memorial and a name better than of sons and of daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off.
echoes.note: 'In my house and within my walls... an everlasting name that will not be cut off' — a name + permanence in the temple, behind 'a pillar in the temple of my God... go out no more' + the inscribed name (3:12). Combines the pillar/temple and new-name motifs.

echoes.text: Lift up your eyes all around, and see: all these gather themselves together, and come to you. As I live,” says Yahweh, “you shall surely clothe yourself with them all as with an ornament, and dress yourself with them, like a bride.
echoes.note: Zion adorned 'like a bride' — faint background to the new Jerusalem coming down (developed fully in Rev 21:2). Diffuse here; stronger later in Revelation.

pericopes.text: “To the angel of the assembly in Laodicea write: “The Amen, the Faithful and True Witness, the Head of God’s creation, says these things: “I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were cold or hot. So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I will vomit you out of my mouth. Because you say, ‘I am rich, and have gotten riches, and have need of nothing;’ and don’t know that you are the wretched one, miserable, poor, blind, and naked; I counsel you to buy from me gold refined by fire, that you may become rich; and white garments, that you may clothe yourself, and that the shame of your nakedness may not be revealed; and eye salve to anoint your eyes, that you may see. As many as I love, I reprove and chasten. Be zealous therefore, and repent. Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him, and will dine with him, and he with me. He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame, and sat down with my Father on his throne. He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.”

echoes.text: My son, don’t despise Yahweh’s discipline, neither be weary of his reproof: for whom Yahweh loves, he reproves; even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.
echoes.note: 'Whom Yahweh loves, he reproves' — directly behind 3:19 'As many as I love, I reprove and chasten.' Very high verbal correspondence (love + reprove/discipline pairing). Rev tracks LXX Prov 3:12 (ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ κύριος παιδεύει), which Hebrews 12:5–6 also cites.

echoes.text: Ephraim said, “Surely I have become rich, I have found myself wealth. In all my wealth they won’t find in me any iniquity that is sin.”
echoes.note: Ephraim's self-deceived boast: 'I have become rich... they won't find in me any iniquity' — the precise prophetic template for Laodicea's 'I am rich... have need of nothing' while truly wretched (3:17). Strong thematic+structural correspondence: false self-assessment of wealth/innocence.

echoes.text: I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will test them like gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will hear them. I will say, ‘It is my people;’ and they will say, ‘Yahweh is my God.’”
echoes.note: Refining the remnant in fire 'as gold is tested' until 'they will call on my name' — behind 'buy from me gold refined by fire' (3:18). Refinement-by-fire + covenant-renewal motif. High thematic coherence.

echoes.text: “Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
echoes.note: 'Come... buy... without money' — the paradox of buying from God without price stands behind the ironic counsel 'buy from me gold' (3:18). Distinctive 'buy' (ἀγοράζω) imperative addressed to the spiritually destitute.

echoes.text: so that he who blesses himself in the earth shall bless himself in the God of truth; and he who swears in the earth shall swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hidden from my eyes.
echoes.note: 'The God of truth' / 'Amen' — Hebrew 'elohe amen behind the self-designation 'The Amen, the Faithful and True Witness' (3:14). Distinctive: Isaiah is the only OT text invoking blessing/oath 'by the God of ’amen.' LXX renders ἀληθινός, losing the 'amen'; Rev preserves the Hebrew ʾmēn, suggesting dependence on the Hebrew.

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
echoes.note: 'The Beginning of God's creation' (3:14) evokes the creation account; ἀρχὴ τῆς κτίσεως plays on Gen 1:1 'In the beginning.' Figural rather than verbal allusion; debated whether Christ is first creature or origin of creation.

echoes.text: “Yahweh possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old.
echoes.note: Personified Wisdom 'in the beginning of his work' — a Wisdom-Christology background to 'the Beginning (ἀρχή) of God's creation' (3:14). Contested: feeds later Arian debates; thematic, not verbatim.

echoes.text: I, Yahweh, search the mind, I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.
echoes.note: 'I, Yahweh, search the mind... give every man according to his ways' — the divine-knowledge formula behind the repeated 'I know your works' (3:15, also 3:1, 3:8). Diffuse across the letters; thematic coherence with judgment by deeds.

echoes.text: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”
echoes.note: 'The voice of my beloved who knocks: Open to me' — a striking verbal parallel to 3:20 'I stand at the door and knock... if anyone... opens the door.' Contested as deliberate allusion vs. shared idiom; volume is notable (knock + open + voice of the beloved).

echoes.text: Yahweh says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”
echoes.note: Enthronement 'sit at my right hand' — background to 'sit down with me on my throne' (3:21). The most-cited NT enthronement psalm; co-regency of the victor mirrors the Son's session. Thematic+structural.

echoes.text: Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
echoes.note: 'Behold, I will do a new thing' — faint resonance with Revelation's pervasive newness (new name, new Jerusalem in 3:12; 'new' here only ambient). Diffuse; included for maximal inventory.

pericopes.text: After these things I looked and saw a door opened in heaven, and the first voice that I heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, was one saying, “Come up here, and I will show you the things which must happen after this.” Immediately I was in the Spirit. Behold, there was a throne set in heaven, and one sitting on the throne that looked like a jasper stone and a sardius. There was a rainbow around the throne, like an emerald to look at.

echoes.text: Above the expanse that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone; and on the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man on it above. I saw as it were glowing metal, as the appearance of fire within it all around, from the appearance of his waist and upward; and from the appearance of his waist and downward I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and there was brightness around him. As […]
echoes.note: Foundational throne-vision template. Volume (Ezekiel's inaugural call vision is the master text behind all of Rev 4-5), verbal recurrence, and structural agreement are all strong: a heavenly throne with One enthroned, surrounded by encircling brightness explicitly likened to a rainbow (iris/qeshet). The gemstone description — sapphire throne, glowing metal, fire all around — supplies the radiant-jewel idiom Revelation translates into jasper, sardius, and emerald. Reticent (Hays): John shows the One on the throne only by mineral light, declining to describe a human form as Ezekiel does (anthropomorphism muted, perhaps deliberately reverential). LXX of Ezek 1:26 uses sappheirou; Rev shifts the stone vocabulary toward Exod 28 breastplate gems.

echoes.text: As the appearance of the rainbow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke.
echoes.note: The rainbow (iris) encircling the throne is a near-verbatim conceptual borrowing of this verse specifically. Distinctive: of all OT theophanies only Ezekiel 1:28 rings the divine glory with a rainbow, so the criterion of distinctiveness is met sharply. LXX renders the Hebrew qeshet with toxon; Rev's iris is the more usual Greek for the meteorological bow (cf. Gen 9 LXX toxon), so John is not slavishly following LXX vocabulary but the image. Also evokes the Noahic covenant bow (Gen 9:13-16) — mercy framing the judgment-throne; listed separately as a contested secondary echo.

echoes.text: I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth. When I bring a cloud over the earth, that the rainbow will be seen in the cloud, and I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the waters will no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The rainbow will be in the cloud. I will look at it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every […]
echoes.note: Contested. The rainbow around the throne may carry the Noahic covenant-of-mercy resonance, softening the throne of judgment with a sign of restraint before the seals open in Rev 6. Thematic coherence is good but verbal volume is low — Rev does not echo Genesis wording, and the primary literary source of the bow image is Ezek 1:28, not Genesis. Held at low confidence as a figural overtone.

echoes.text: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these: as for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what shall happen.
echoes.note: “I will show you the things which must happen after this” (ha dei genesthai meta tauta) reproduces the apocalyptic-disclosure formula of Daniel 2:28-29 LXX/Theodotion (ha dei genesthai... — what God reveals as what must take place). The Greek dei (divine necessity) plus the temporal phrase is verbally distinctive and recurs as a structural frame across Revelation (1:1; 1:19; 22:6). Theodotion's Daniel is the closer textual base than the OG. The formula reframes the whole vision as Danielic unveiling of the determined future.

echoes.text: On the third day, when it was morning, there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet; and all the people who were in the camp trembled.
echoes.note: The summoning “voice... like a trumpet” recalls the Sinai theophany, where the trumpet blast accompanies God's self-revelation atop the mountain. Coherence with the broader Sinai background of Rev 4 (the thunder/lightning of v.5 also draws on this verse) strengthens the link; the trumpet-as-divine-voice is a recurring Sinai motif (cf. Exod 20:18; Heb 12:19). Medium because the trumpet in Rev 1:10/4:1 may primarily be conventional apocalyptic angelophany rather than a deliberate Sinai citation.

echoes.text: Micaiah said, “Therefore hear Yahweh’s word. I saw Yahweh sitting on his throne, and all the army of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.
echoes.note: Micaiah's throne-council vision — “I saw Yahweh sitting on his throne” with the heavenly host attending — is one of the canonical divine-council scenes that stands behind Rev 4's enthroned One surrounded by attendant beings. Recurrence of the prophetic throne-vision type-scene; shares vocabulary of seeing the LORD seated (kathemenon epi tou thronou). Medium: the council/host motif is fully developed in vv.4-10, so this verse is more a generic backdrop than a pinpoint source for vv.1-3.

pericopes.text: Around the throne were twenty-four thrones. On the thrones were twenty-four elders sitting, dressed in white garments, with crowns of gold on their heads. Out of the throne proceed lightnings, sounds, and thunders. There were seven lamps of fire burning before his throne, which are the seven Spirits of God. Before the throne was something like a sea of glass, similar to crystal. In the midst of the throne, and around the throne were four living creatures full of eyes before and behind.

echoes.text: On the third day, when it was morning, there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet; and all the people who were in the camp trembled.
echoes.note: “Out of the throne proceed lightnings, sounds, and thunders” is a direct Sinai-theophany cluster: astrapai kai phonai kai brontai is the fixed triad Revelation repeats at every major hinge (4:5; 8:5; 11:19; 16:18), and it derives from the thunders-and-lightnings of the Sinai descent. Distinctive and recurrent: the three-fold storm formula is a signature Revelation idiom rooting the throne in the mountain of the giving of the Law. LXX Exod 19:16 has phonai kai astrapai — the same lexemes John reorders. Strong on volume and recurrence.

echoes.text: They saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was like a paved work of sapphire stone, like the skies for clearness.
echoes.note: The “sea of glass, similar to crystal” before the throne echoes the pavement under God's feet at Sinai — “like a paved work of sapphire stone, like the skies for clearness” — the transparent, sky-clear floor of the divine presence. Coherence and distinctiveness: a crystalline transparent expanse beneath/before God is rare and concentrated here and in Ezek 1:22. LXX Exod 24:10 reads hosei ergon plinthou sappheirou kai hosper eidos stereomatos tou ouranou — the firmament-clearness John captures with hyalini... homoia krystallo. Pairs with Ezek 1:22 as joint source.

echoes.text: Over the head of the living creature there was the likeness of an expanse, like the awesome crystal to look on, stretched out over their heads above.
echoes.note: “Sea of glass, similar to crystal” draws the word crystal (krystallos) directly from Ezekiel's firmament “like an awesome crystal” spread over the living creatures' heads. Verbal distinctiveness is high: krystallos is the rare shared term, and Ezekiel's expanse stands in the same throne-vision John is reworking, so coherence is total. John relocates the crystalline expanse from above the creatures (Ezek) to before the throne (a sea), combining it with the Sinai pavement (Exod 24:10). LXX Ezek 1:22 uses krystallos, so John follows the Greek lexeme closely.

echoes.text: He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I have seen, and behold, a lamp stand all of gold, with its bowl on the top of it, and its seven lamps on it; there are seven pipes to each of the lamps, which are on the top of it;
echoes.note: The “seven lamps of fire burning before his throne” identified as “the seven Spirits of God” fuses Zechariah's golden lampstand of seven lamps with his interpretation (Zech 4:6, 'not by might... but by my Spirit') and the sevenfold spirit of Isa 11:2. Distinctiveness: seven lamps explicitly equated with the divine Spirit(s) is a uniquely Zecharian configuration. NOTE: this verse's text could not be retrieved verbatim from bible-api.com (repeated HTTP 429); the bracketed WEB text is supplied from the World English Bible but was NOT fetched live and should be re-verified. Strong on coherence and recurrence (Rev 1:4; 5:6 also use the seven Spirits/seven lamps).

echoes.text: Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed; for Yahweh of Armies will reign on Mount Zion, and in Jerusalem; and before his elders will be glory.
echoes.note: Contested source for the twenty-four enthroned “elders.” Isaiah envisions Yahweh reigning “before his elders... in glory,” the only OT throne-text that explicitly seats elders in the divine presence-glory (cf. Exod 24:9-10, the seventy elders who see God). Thematic coherence is suggestive — enthroned elders around the reigning LORD — but verbal volume is thin and the number twenty-four (24 priestly/Levitical courses, 1 Chr 24-25; or 12+12) is not from Isaiah. Held at low/contested.

echoes.text: The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.
echoes.note: The “seven Spirits of God” likely also draws on the sevenfold enumeration of the Spirit resting on the Davidic shoot (LXX Isa 11:2 lists seven spirit-gifts, expanding the Hebrew six with an added 'piety'). Coherence with Revelation's seven-Spirits theology is good. NOTE: text supplied from WEB but NOT fetched live (rate-limit avoidance); flagged for verification. The LXX-vs-Hebrew divergence is itself the basis of the 'seven' (Hebrew has six pairs); John's sevenfold count tracks the Greek tradition.

pericopes.text: The first creature was like a lion, and the second creature like a calf, and the third creature had a face like a man, and the fourth was like a flying eagle. The four living creatures, each one of them having six wings, are full of eyes around and within. They have no rest day and night, saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come!” When the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to him who sits on the throne, to him who lives forever and ever, the twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne, and worship him who lives forever and ever, and throw their crowns before the throne, saying, “Worthy are you, our Lord and God, the Holy One, to receive the glory, the honor, and the power, for you created all things, and because of your desire they existed, and were created!”

echoes.text: Out of its midst came the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: they had the likeness of a man. Everyone had four faces, and each one of them had four wings. Their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf’s foot; and they sparkled like burnished brass. They had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and the four of them had their faces and their wings thus: their wings were […]
echoes.note: The “four living creatures” (tessara zoa) with the faces of lion, ox/calf, man, and eagle is a direct dependence on Ezekiel's four living creatures (LXX zoa). Volume, distinctiveness, and recurrence are maximal: the very phrase 'living creatures' and the exact four faces are Ezekiel's. John redistributes the faces (Ezekiel: each creature has all four faces; Rev: each creature bears one face) and substitutes 'calf/ox' (Ezek 'ox', moschos in LXX = Rev 'calf'). LXX Ezek 1:10 supplies the lexical set. The cherubic creatures become heavenly worship-leaders in Revelation.

echoes.text: In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple. Above him stood the seraphim. Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew. One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!” The foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who called, and the house was […]
echoes.note: The Trisagion — “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty” — and the six wings are lifted from Isaiah's seraphim. Distinctiveness and volume are at their peak: the threefold 'Holy' (LXX hagios hagios hagios) and the six wings (hex pteryges) are Isaiah's signature, found nowhere else in this configuration. John conflates Isaiah's six-winged seraphim with Ezekiel's four-faced cherubim (eyes all around) into a single composite order. 'Lord God Almighty' (kyrios ho theos ho pantokrator) renders the Hebrew 'Yahweh of Armies / Yahweh Sabaoth' that LXX often gives as kyrios sabaoth or pantokrator. Echo of glory-filling-the-earth underlies Rev's cosmic doxology.

echoes.text: Their whole body, and their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes all around, even the wheels that the four of them had.
echoes.note: “Full of eyes before and behind... around and within” draws the eyes-all-around motif from Ezekiel 10:12 (the second cherubim vision), where the creatures' whole bodies and wheels are full of eyes. Distinctiveness is high — bodies covered in eyes is a peculiarly Ezekielan detail. John transfers the eyes from the wheels/bodies (Ezek 1:18; 10:12) onto the wings/bodies of the creatures themselves. Pairs with Ezek 1:18 below as the dual source of the eyes.

echoes.text: As for their rims, they were high and dreadful; and the four of them had their rims full of eyes all around.
echoes.note: Companion source to Ezek 10:12 for the “full of eyes” detail; here the eyes are on the rims of the wheels, 'full of eyes all around' (kykloi auton, plereis ophthalmon in LXX). The phrase 'full of eyes all around' (gemonta ophthalmon kyklothen) in Rev 4:8 echoes this Greek closely. Distinctive, recurrent within Ezekiel, and verbally tight.

echoes.text: At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored him who lives forever; for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom from generation to generation.
echoes.note: “Him who lives forever and ever” (to zonti eis tous aionas ton aionon) is the Danielic divine title for the eternally-living God whom even Nebuchadnezzar blesses (Dan 4:34; cf. Dan 6:26; 12:7). Distinctiveness: this 'the one who lives forever' formula is a hallmark of Daniel and the Second-Temple liturgical vocabulary Revelation inherits. Theodotion Dan 4:34 has zonti eis ton aiona; Rev expands to the plural-of-eternity. Coherent with Revelation's repeated use of the title (1:18; 10:6; 15:7).

echoes.text: Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, Yahweh, the first, and with the last, I am he.”
echoes.note: The title “who was and who is and who is to come” paraphrases the divine self-identification of Deutero-Isaiah — 'I, Yahweh, the first... and the last, I am he' — the eternity formula Revelation triples into past-present-future (cf. Isa 44:6; 48:12). Coherence is strong with Revelation's Alpha-and-Omega theology, but the threefold temporal expansion is John's own (likely shaped by Hellenistic-Jewish renderings of the divine Name / Exod 3:14 'I am who I am' tradition). Medium: conceptual, not verbal, dependence on this specific verse.

echoes.text: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and he said, “You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
echoes.note: “Who was and who is and who is to come” is widely read as a temporal paraphrase of the divine Name revealed at the bush — the ehyeh / 'I AM' of Exod 3:14 — expanded across the three tenses in line with Targumic and Hellenistic-Jewish triple-time glosses of the Tetragrammaton. Coherence is high; this is a contested-but-common scholarly identification. NOTE: text supplied from WEB, NOT fetched live (rate-limit avoidance) — flag for verification. LXX Exod 3:14 ego eimi ho on ('the Being One') is itself the ontological reading Rev's formula presupposes.

echoes.text: You are Yahweh, even you alone. You have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their army, the earth and all things that are on it, the seas and all that is in them, and you preserve them all. The army of heaven worships you.
echoes.note: The creation-doxology — “you created all things... they existed, and were created,” worshiped by the heavenly host — strongly parallels the Levites' confession: 'You alone... made heaven... the earth and all things on it... and the army of heaven worships you.' Coherence and structural agreement are excellent: God as sole Creator of all, adored by the heavenly army, is exactly the logic of Rev 4:11. Distinctive shared move: the worth/worship of God grounded precisely in his having created and preserved all things. LXX 2 Esdras 19:6 supplies the Greek base.

echoes.text: By Yahweh’s word, the heavens were made; all their army by the breath of his mouth. He gathers the waters of the sea together as a heap. He lays up the deeps in storehouses. Let all the earth fear Yahweh. Let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him. For he spoke, and it was done. He commanded, and it stood firm.
echoes.note: “Because of your desire they existed, and were created” echoes the creation-by-the-word/will theology of Ps 33 — 'he spoke, and it was done; he commanded, and it stood firm.' The link between God's will/word and things coming into being is the conceptual engine of Rev 4:11b. LXX Ps 32:9 autos eipen kai egenethesan, autos eneteilato kai ektisthesan — note ektisthesan ('they were created'), the very verb Rev 4:11 ends on. Strong verbal coherence in the Greek; God's bare will effecting creation.

echoes.text: Of old, you laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the work of your hands.
echoes.note: Supports the creation-doxology of v.11 — God as the one who 'laid the foundation of the earth' and whose hands made the heavens — part of the OT creator-praise pool (cf. Ps 8; Ps 95:5; Ps 146:6) on which Rev 4:11 draws. Medium because it is general creator-language rather than a pinpoint verbal source; Neh 9:6 and Ps 33:6-9 are the closer parallels. LXX Ps 101:26 kat' archas su... ten gen ethemeliosas.

echoes.text: [source text not in the World English Bible]
echoes.note: Second-Temple parallel: the unsleeping watchers ceaselessly chanting the Trisagion before God's glory — strikingly close to Rev 4:8's creatures who 'have no rest day and night' singing 'Holy, holy, holy.' Demonstrates that John works within a living apocalyptic liturgical tradition (Isa 6 mediated through Enochic worship-scenes), not Isaiah alone. Low confidence by editorial convention (non-canonical, not fetchable in WEB) but historically a high-value coherence parallel for the ceaseless angelic Sanctus. LXX-vs-Hebrew not applicable; Greek/Ethiopic Enoch tradition.

echoes.text: I saw until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire. A fiery stream issued and came out from before him: thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
echoes.note: The throne-and-courtroom setting with multiple thrones (Dan 7:9 'thrones were placed') and the surrounding myriads who serve and worship (Dan 7:10) lies behind the assembled worship of Rev 4:9-11 and the twenty-four thrones of v.4. Coherence with Revelation's pervasive Danielic frame is strong; the plural 'thrones' is distinctive. Medium for this pericope because the explicit creatures/Trisagion are from Ezekiel/Isaiah; Daniel 7 most directly governs the enthronement and the surrounding council. Theodotion Dan 7:9-10 supplies the Greek throne-of-fire imagery.

pericopes.text: I saw, in the right hand of him who sat on the throne, a book written inside and outside, sealed shut with seven seals. I saw a mighty angel proclaiming with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the book, and to break its seals?” No one in heaven above, or on the earth, or under the earth, was able to open the book, or to look in it. And I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open the book, or to look in it. One of the elders said to me, “Don’t weep. Behold, the Lion who is of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has overcome; he who opens the book and its seven seals.”

echoes.text: When I looked, behold, a hand was stretched out to me; and, behold, a scroll of a book was therein; He spread it before me: and it was written within and without; and there were written therein lamentations, and mourning, and woe.
echoes.note: Hays: high verbal volume — the rare detail of a scroll 'written inside and outside / within and without' is shared almost verbatim, and the prophetic-call setting (a heavenly hand presenting a written-on-both-sides scroll to the seer) is recurrent. John conflates Ezekiel's two-sided scroll with Daniel's sealing. The double-sided writing signals a complete, fixed decree with no room left to add. WEB Greek 'gegrammenon esōthen kai opisthen' tracks the Hebrew 'written within and without'; LXX Ezekiel renders similarly.

echoes.text: But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run back and forth, and knowledge shall be increased.”
echoes.note: Hays: thematic + verbal coherence — the motif of a 'sealed book' (sphragizō / sealed) reserved 'to the time of the end' supplies the eschatological logic of Revelation 5: the sealed scroll contains the end-time decree that only the worthy one may unseal. Daniel 12 is the closest source for sealing a book until the appointed time; cf. also Daniel 8:26; 12:9. Septuagint/Theodotion both use sphragizō, matching Revelation's vocabulary.

echoes.text: Judah is a lion’s cub. From the prey, my son, you have gone up. He stooped down, he crouched as a lion, as a lioness. Who will rouse him up? The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom it belongs. To him will the obedience of the peoples be.
echoes.note: Hays: high — explicit messianic title 'the Lion who is of the tribe of Judah' draws directly on Jacob's blessing, the foundational text linking Judah to a lion and to enduring rule ('scepter will not depart'). Early Jewish/Christian reading took 'until he comes to whom it belongs' (Shiloh) messianically. The lion of Judah and the unfailing scepter together yield the conquering ruler John names. LXX 'heōs an elthē ta apokeimena autō' was read messianically in Second Temple sources.

echoes.text: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.
echoes.note: Hays: high — the second title in 5:5, 'the Root of David,' fuses Isaiah's 'shoot/branch from the stock of Jesse' (11:1) and 'the root of Jesse' to whom 'the nations will seek' (11:10). John transposes 'root of Jesse' to 'Root of David' (cf. Revelation 22:16), keeping the Davidic-messianic 'rizah Iessai' of LXX Isaiah 11:10, which Paul also cites (Romans 15:12). Pairing Lion-of-Judah with Root-of-David binds Genesis 49 and Isaiah 11 into one messianic identity.

echoes.text: All vision has become to you like the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one who is educated, saying, “Read this, please”; and he says, “I can’t, for it is sealed:”
echoes.note: Hays: medium — supplies the precise scene of a sealed book that no one is able to read/open, with the futile search for a reader echoing John's search for one 'worthy to open the book.' Reinforces the Ezekiel/Daniel scroll cluster: revelation is locked until the qualified one breaks the seal. Verbal link is the sealed-book ('sepher chatum') unable to be opened.

echoes.text: Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the pride of the Jordan against the strong habitation: for I will suddenly make them run away from it; and whoever is chosen, him will I appoint over it: for who is like me? and who will appoint me a time? and who is the shepherd who will stand before me?
echoes.note: Hays: low / contested — lion-of-conquest imagery is widespread (Jer 49:19; 50:44; Hos 11:10; Amos 3:8), so the 'Lion' of 5:5 need not depend on any one beyond Genesis 49. Listed as a faint reinforcing background to the lion motif, not a primary source; Genesis 49 remains the controlling intertext. Marked low because verbal specificity is lacking and the phrase here is not the fetched WEB wording.

pericopes.text: I saw in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain, having seven horns, and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God, sent out into all the earth. Then he came, and he took it out of the right hand of him who sat on the throne. Now when he had taken the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each one having a harp, and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.

echoes.text: He was oppressed, yet when he was afflicted he didn’t open his mouth. As a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that before its shearers is mute, so he didn’t open his mouth.
echoes.note: Hays: high — 'a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain' draws on the Servant who is silently 'led to the slaughter' like a lamb. The redemptive-by-death logic that grounds the Lamb's worthiness is Isaiah 53's vicarious suffering. Note lexical divergence: Revelation favors 'arnion' for the slain Lamb, while LXX Isaiah 53:7 uses 'probaton/amnos'; the figural link is conceptual (sacrificial slaughter) more than verbatim, which is why the Passover lamb is a co-source.

echoes.text: Your lamb shall be without defect, a male a year old. You shall take it from the sheep, or from the goats: and you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at evening.
echoes.note: Hays: high (figural) — the slain-yet-standing Lamb evokes the Passover lamb slaughtered by 'the whole assembly,' whose blood redeems (Exod 12:13). Combined with 5:9 ('bought us... with your blood, out of every... nation'), the new-exodus/Passover typology is unmistakable. The Lamb's death effects a redemption patterned on Passover deliverance from Egypt.

echoes.text: Indeed, who despises the day of small things? For these seven shall rejoice, and shall see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. These are the eyes of Yahweh, which run back and forth through the whole earth.”
echoes.note: Hays: high — the Lamb's 'seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God, sent out into all the earth' is a near-citation of Zechariah's 'seven... these are Yahweh's eyes, which run... through the whole earth.' John identifies the seven eyes with the sevenfold Spirit, fusing Zechariah's omniscient divine eyes with the lampstand vision (Zech 4:2). Strong verbal recurrence of 'seven' + 'eyes' + 'whole/all the earth.'

echoes.text: He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I have seen, and behold, a lamp stand all of gold, with its bowl on the top of it, and its seven lamps on it; there are seven pipes to each of the lamps, which are on the top of it;
echoes.note: Hays: medium — the wider Zechariah 4 lampstand vision underlies John's identification of the 'seven eyes' with 'the seven Spirits of God': the seven lamps and the explanatory 'by my Spirit' link the sevenfold lamps to the divine Spirit. Reinforces 5:6 and the 'seven Spirits' motif of Revelation 1:4; 3:1; 4:5.
