His servants carried him in a chariot dead from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb. The people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in his father’s place.
echoes.note: Josiah slain by Pharaoh Necho at Megiddo — the archetypal catastrophe at that site feeding 'Megiddo/Har-Magedon' (16:16) as a name for definitive defeat. Historical-typological.

echoes.text: In that day there will be a great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon.
echoes.note: 'The mourning of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo' — Megiddo as a place of great mourning/defeat, contributing to the symbolic 'Megiddo/Har-Magedon' of 16:16. Onomastic source.

echoes.text: “The kings came and fought, then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo. They took no plunder of silver.
echoes.note: 'The kings came and fought... at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo' — the Song of Deborah's battle of kings at Megiddo where the LORD routs the foe; archetype for the kings gathered at Megiddo (16:16).

echoes.text: But news out of the east and out of the north shall trouble him; and he shall go out with great fury to destroy and utterly to sweep away many.
echoes.note: 'Tidings from the east' alarm the king; the 'kings from the sunrise' (16:12) may draw on the eastern-invader threat motif. Faint.

echoes.text: He will pass through the sea of affliction, and will strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up; and the pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart.
echoes.note: 'The depths of the Nile shall dry up' — another drying-of-waters new-Exodus motif feeding the Euphrates' drying (16:12). Faint, cited in brief.

echoes.text: Their eyes were opened, and they both knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves. They heard the voice of Yahweh God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Yahweh God among the trees of the garden. Yahweh God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?” The man said, “I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I […]
echoes.note: Shame of nakedness / being seen naked underlies 'keeps his clothes, so that he doesn't walk naked, and they see his shame' (16:15). Faint, thematic.

pericopes.text: The seventh poured out his bowl into the air. A loud voice came out of the temple of heaven, from the throne, saying, “It is done!” There were lightnings, sounds, and thunders; and there was a great earthquake, such as was not since there were men on the earth, so great an earthquake, so mighty. The great city was divided into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. Babylon the great was remembered in the sight of God, to give to her the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath. Every island fled away, and the mountains were not found. Great hailstones, about the weight of a talent, came down out of the sky on people. People blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, for this plague is exceedingly severe.

echoes.text: On the third day, when it was morning, there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet; and all the people who were in the camp trembled. Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the lower part of the mountain. Mount Sinai, all it, smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked […]
echoes.note: Sinai theophany: thunders, lightnings, and the whole mountain quaking greatly. The seventh bowl's 'lightnings, sounds, thunders, and a great earthquake' (16:18) is patterned on the covenant-making theophany, now as covenant judgment.

echoes.text: For in my jealousy and in the fire of my wrath have I spoken, Surely in that day there shall be a great shaking in the land of Israel; so that the fish of the sea, and the birds of the sky, and the animals of the field, and all creeping things who creep on the earth, and all the men who are on the surface of the earth, shall shake at my presence, and the mountains shall be thrown down, and the steep places shall fall, and every wall shall fall to the […]
echoes.note: Gog oracle: 'a great earthquake... the mountains shall be thrown down,' all creatures quake at God's presence. Direct source for the unprecedented earthquake and mountains/islands fleeing (16:18,20).

echoes.text: With pestilence and with blood will I enter into judgment with him; and I will rain on him, and on his hordes, and on the many peoples who are with him, an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, fire, and sulfur.
echoes.note: Against Gog: 'I will rain... great hailstones, fire, and sulfur.' Primary source for the talent-weight hailstones of bowl 7 (16:21), tied to the same Gog judgment as the earthquake.

echoes.text: For thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, to me: take this cup of the wine of wrath at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send you, to drink it. They shall drink, and reel back and forth, and be mad, because of the sword that I will send among them.
echoes.note: 'Take this cup of the wine of wrath... make all the nations drink it.' Source for Babylon being given 'the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath' (16:19); the wrath-cup oracle that names Babylon's draught.

echoes.text: Awake, awake, stand up, Jerusalem, that have drunk at the hand of Yahweh the cup of his wrath; you have drunken the bowl of the cup of staggering, and drained it.
echoes.note: 'You who have drunk... the cup of his wrath, the bowl of staggering.' Reinforces the wrath-cup imagery applied to Babylon (16:19); verbal cup-of-wrath chain shared with Jer 25 and Rev 14:10.

echoes.text: As they fled from before Israel, while they were at the descent of Beth Horon, Yahweh hurled down great stones from the sky on them to Azekah, and they died. There were more who died from the hailstones than who the children of Israel killed with the sword.
echoes.note: The LORD casts great hailstones from heaven on the fleeing kings — 'more died from the hailstones than... by the sword.' Holy-war hail against enemy kings underlies the lethal hail of 16:21.

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
echoes.note: 'A time of trouble such as never was since there was a nation.' The 'unprecedented' formula of the earthquake 'such as was not since there were men' (16:18) draws on Daniel's superlative-tribulation language.

echoes.text: Thus says your Lord Yahweh, and your God who pleads the cause of his people, “Behold, I have taken out of your hand the cup of staggering, even the bowl of the cup of my wrath; you shall no more drink it again: and I will put it into the hand of those who afflict you, who have said to your soul, ‘Bow down, that we may walk over you;’ and you have laid your back as the ground, and as the street, to those who walk over.”
echoes.note: The wrath-cup taken from Zion and put 'into the hand of your tormentors' — the reversal whereby the oppressor (Babylon) now drinks the cup; supports the Babylon-remembered judgment of 16:19.

echoes.text: Men shall go into the caves of the rocks, and into the holes of the earth, from before the terror of Yahweh, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.
echoes.note: Men flee 'when he arises to terrify the earth'; mountains and the proud brought low. The fleeing islands and vanished mountains (16:20) draw on the Day-of-the-LORD cosmic-upheaval motif. Cf. Isa 40:4.

echoes.text: I saw the earth, and, behold, it was waste and void; and the heavens, and they had no light. I saw the mountains, and behold, they trembled, and all the hills moved back and forth. I saw, and behold, there was no man, and all the birds of the sky had fled. I saw, and behold, the fruitful field was a wilderness, and all its cities were broken down at the presence of Yahweh, before his fierce anger.
echoes.note: Cosmic de-creation: mountains quaking, hills moving, no man left. Reinforces the dissolution of mountains/islands (16:20) as un-creation judgment. Faint.

pericopes.text: One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying, “Come here. I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute who sits on many waters, with whom the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality, and those who dwell in the earth were made drunken with the wine of her sexual immorality.” He carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness. I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet-colored animal, full of blasphemous names, having seven heads and ten horns. The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and the impurities of the sexual immorality of the earth. And on her forehead a name was written, “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF THE PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus. When I saw her, I wondered with great amazement.

echoes.text: You who dwell on many waters, abundant in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your covetousness.
echoes.note: Babylon apostrophized as 'you who dwell on many waters, abundant in treasures' — the unique source for the harlot 'who sits on many waters,' transposed from Babylon's literal Euphrates canals onto the symbolic seat of Rome. Hays: volume, recurrence (Babylon-oracle of Jer 50–51 anchors Rev 17–18), thematic coherence (judgment of Babylon). LXX Jer 28:13.

echoes.text: Babylon has been a golden cup in Yahweh’s hand, who made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunk of her wine; therefore the nations are mad.
echoes.note: 'Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand, making all the earth drunken; the nations drank of her wine, therefore the nations are mad' — direct verbal-conceptual template for the golden cup in her hand and the nations made drunk with the wine of her fornication. Hays: volume (golden cup + drunkenness + nations), distinctiveness. LXX Jer 28:7.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s word came again to me, saying, Son of man, there were two women, the daughters of one mother: and they played the prostitute in Egypt; they played the prostitute in their youth; there were their breasts pressed, and there was handled the bosom of their virginity. Their names were Oholah the elder, and Oholibah her sister: and they became mine, and they bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem Oholibah. Oholah […]
echoes.note: Oholah/Oholibah (Samaria/Jerusalem) as two harlot sisters arrayed in finery, fornicating with the nations and their kings, judged by their former lovers — the controlling type for the harlot-city dressed in purple/scarlet and gold who commits fornication with the kings of the earth. Hays: thematic coherence, recurrence across Rev 17.

echoes.text: Again Yahweh’s word came to me, saying, Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations; and say, Thus says the Lord Yahweh to Jerusalem: Your birth and your birth is of the land of the Canaanite; the Amorite was your father, and your mother was a Hittite. As for your birth, in the day you were born your navel was not cut, neither were you washed in water to cleanse you; you weren’t salted at all, nor swaddled at all. No eye pitied you, to do any of […]
echoes.note: Jerusalem the harlot decked by God with gold, fine linen, embroidered cloth and jewels, then prostituting herself to every passerby and judged by stripping and burning (cf. 16:39) — source of the harlot's adornment (gold, precious stones) and the whole adulterous-city schema. Hays: volume, coherence with v.16's stripping/burning.

echoes.text: Take a harp; go about the city, you prostitute that has been forgotten. Make sweet melody. Sing many songs, that you may be remembered. It will happen after the end of seventy years that Yahweh will visit Tyre, and she shall return to her wages, and will play the prostitute with all the kingdoms of the world on the surface of the earth.
echoes.note: Tyre the forgotten harlot who 'plays the harlot with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth' and gathers her hire — closest OT parallel to 'the kings of the earth committed fornication' with the merchant-harlot (developed in Rev 18). Hays: distinctive 'harlotry with the kingdoms of the earth' phrase.

echoes.text: because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft.
echoes.note: Nineveh, 'the well-favored harlot, mistress of sorceries, who sells nations through her harlotry' — the harlot-imperial-city betraying nations by her seductions; reinforces the wine-of-fornication-intoxicates-the-nations motif. Hays: thematic coherence, recurrence of harlot-city topos.

echoes.text: The king spoke and said, Is not this great Babylon, which I have built for the royal dwelling place, by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?
echoes.note: Nebuchadnezzar's boast 'Is not this great Babylon, which I have built?' — the title 'Babylon the great' likely crystallizes from this Danielic phrase (Aramaic Dan 4:27 MT). Hays: distinctive collocation 'Babylon the great.'

echoes.text: After this I saw in the night visions, and, behold, a fourth animal, awesome and powerful, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth; it devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet: and it was diverse from all the animals that were before it; and it had ten horns.
echoes.note: Daniel's fourth beast, 'terrible, dreadful... and it had ten horns' — source of the beast 'having seven heads and ten horns'; the ten horns are explicitly the Danielic kings (cf. v.12). Hays: volume, distinctiveness of ten-horned beast.

echoes.text: I considered the horns, and behold, there came up among them another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots: and behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.
echoes.note: The little horn with 'a mouth speaking great things' (blasphemies, cf. 7:25) feeds the beast 'full of blasphemous names.' Hays: thematic coherence with Daniel's blaspheming horn.

echoes.text: Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and save every man his life; don’t be cut off in her iniquity: for it is the time of Yahweh’s vengeance; he will render to her a recompense.
echoes.note: 'Flee out of the midst of Babylon... be not cut off in her iniquity, for this is the time of the LORD's vengeance' frames the judgment-of-Babylon oracle the angel announces ('the judgment of the great prostitute'). Hays: recurrence within the same Jeremianic source-block. LXX Jer 28:6.

echoes.text: The burden of the wilderness of the sea. As whirlwinds in the South sweep through, it comes from the wilderness, from an awesome land. A grievous vision is declared to me. The treacherous man deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam; attack! I have stopped all of Media’s sighing. Therefore my thighs are filled with anguish. Pains have taken hold on me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am in so much pain that I can’t hear. I so am […]
echoes.note: The oracle 'concerning the wilderness of the sea' culminating in 'Fallen, fallen is Babylon' — the prophet 'carried away in the Spirit into a wilderness' to view Babylon's fall may draw the wilderness-vision setting from this Babylon oracle. Hays: thematic coherence (wilderness + Babylon's fall, cf. Rev 18:2). LXX Isa 21:1.

echoes.text: For thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, to me: take this cup of the wine of wrath at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send you, to drink it.
echoes.note: 'Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand and cause all the nations to drink' — the cup-makes-the-nations-drink imagery overlaps the harlot's golden cup; the wine here is wrath but the structure feeds Revelation's cup symbolism. Hays: coherence with Rev's wine/cup of wrath fusion. LXX Jer 32:15.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s word came again to me, saying, You, son of man, take up a lamentation over Tyre; and tell Tyre, you who dwell at the entry of the sea, who are the merchant of the peoples to many islands, thus says the Lord Yahweh: You, Tyre, have said, I am perfect in beauty. Your borders are in the heart of the seas; your builders have perfected your beauty. They have made all your planks of fir trees from Senir; they have taken a cedar from Lebanon to make a […]
echoes.note: Tyre's lament cataloguing purple, fine linen, gold, precious stones, pearls and merchandise undergirds the harlot's wardrobe of purple/scarlet, gold, precious stones and pearls (more fully in Rev 18). Hays: shared luxury-catalogue vocabulary.

echoes.text: She took off of her the garments of her widowhood, and covered herself with her veil, and wrapped herself, and sat in the gate of Enaim, which is by the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah was grown up, and she wasn’t given to him as a wife.
echoes.note: Tamar's harlot disguise establishes the biblical harlot's veil/adornment idiom; faint, generic background to the dressed-and-decked prostitute. Hays: low distinctiveness.

echoes.text: Behold, there a woman met him with the attire of a prostitute, and with crafty intent.
echoes.note: The adorned harlot with seductive attire who waylays the simple — wisdom-tradition coloring of the bedecked prostitute. Faint, thematic only.

echoes.text: For in the hand of Yahweh there is a cup, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours it out. Indeed the wicked of the earth drink and drink it to its very dregs.
echoes.note: 'In the hand of the LORD is a cup of foaming wine... all the wicked of the earth shall drink it' — the cup-in-hand making the earth drink; reinforces the cup/intoxication network behind the harlot's golden cup. Hays: coherence, low distinctiveness. LXX Ps 74:9.

echoes.text: I saw, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them;
echoes.note: The horn 'made war with the saints and prevailed against them' colors 'the woman drunken with the blood of the saints' — Babylon/the beast slaughtering the holy ones. Faint here, fuller at Rev 13:7. Hays: thematic coherence.

pericopes.text: The angel said to me, “Why do you wonder? I will tell you the mystery of the woman, and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns. The beast that you saw was, and is not; and is about to come up out of the abyss and to go into destruction. Those who dwell on the earth and whose names have not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world will marvel when they see that the beast was, and is not, and shall be present. Here is the mind that has wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman sits. They are seven kings. Five have fallen, the one is, the other has not yet come. When he comes, he must continue a little while. The beast that was, and is not, is himself also an eighth, and is of the seven; and he goes to destruction.

echoes.text: Four great animals came up from the sea, diverse one from another.
echoes.note: 'Four great beasts came up from the sea' supplies the beast that 'comes up out of the abyss'; Daniel's sea/deep becomes John's abyss as the chaos-source of imperial beasts. Hays: volume, recurrence across Rev 11:7; 13:1; 17:8. LXX/Theodotion Dan 7:3.

echoes.text: I saw at that time because of the voice of the great words which the horn spoke; I saw even until the animal was slain, and its body destroyed, and it was given to be burned with fire.
echoes.note: The fourth beast 'slain and its body destroyed and given to the burning flame' — direct source for the beast that 'goes into destruction' (twice in this unit). Hays: thematic coherence (beast's appointed destruction), distinctiveness.

echoes.text: These great animals, which are four, are four kings, who shall arise out of the earth.
echoes.note: 'These great beasts... are four kings that shall arise' grounds the interpretive equation 'the seven heads... are seven kings.' Hays: the Danielic beast-equals-kings hermeneutic is reused. Theodotion Dan 7:17.

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
echoes.note: Those 'written in the book' shall be delivered — antithesis to 'whose names have not been written in the book of life.' Hays: coherence with Daniel's book-of-deliverance at the end. LXX/Theodotion Dan 12:1.

echoes.text: Yet now, if you will, forgive their sin—and if not, please blot me out of your book which you have written.” Yahweh said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.
echoes.note: 'Blot me out of your book which you have written... whoever has sinned I will blot out' — the originating 'book' of the living/registered, behind 'the book of life.' Hays: distinctive book-of-life lemma. LXX Exod 32:32.

echoes.text: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, and not be written with the righteous.
echoes.note: 'Let them be blotted out of the book of the living and not be written with the righteous' — the closest phrase to names (not) written in the book of life. Hays: distinctiveness of 'book of the living.' LXX Ps 68:29.

echoes.text: He changes the times and the seasons; he removes kings, and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who have understanding;
echoes.note: God 'removes kings and sets up kings' and gives 'wisdom to the wise' — backdrop to the rise-and-fall sequence of kings and the call for the 'mind that has wisdom.' Faint, thematic. Theodotion Dan 2:21.

echoes.text: He shall speak words against the Most High, and shall wear out the saints of the Most High; and he shall think to change the times and the law; and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time.
echoes.note: 'He shall... continue for a time, times and half a time' — the appointed limited span colors 'he must continue a little while.' Faint structural parallel of bounded time. Hays: low.

pericopes.text: The ten horns that you saw are ten kings who have received no kingdom as yet, but they receive authority as kings, with the beast, for one hour. These have one mind, and they give their power and authority to the beast. These will war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings, and those who are with him are called, chosen, and faithful.”

echoes.text: As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom shall ten kings arise: and another shall arise after them; and he shall be diverse from the former, and he shall put down three kings.
echoes.note: 'The ten horns are ten kings that shall arise' — the explicit, near-verbatim source for 'the ten horns... are ten kings.' Hays: volume, distinctiveness, recurrence. Theodotion Dan 7:24.

echoes.text: and concerning the ten horns that were on its head, and the other horn which came up, and before which three fell, even that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spoke great things, whose look was more stout than its fellows.
echoes.note: The 'ten horns on its head' and the horn that 'made war with the saints' inform the ten-horns-with-the-beast warring imagery here turned against the Lamb. Hays: coherence with Daniel's horn-king war motif.

echoes.text: For Yahweh your God, he is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the awesome, who doesn’t respect persons, nor takes reward.
echoes.note: 'The LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords' — primary OT source for the Lamb as 'Lord of lords.' Divine title transferred to the Lamb. Hays: distinctive divine title, recurrence at Rev 19:16. LXX Deut 10:17.

echoes.text: The king answered to Daniel, and said, Of a truth your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.
echoes.note: Nebuchadnezzar confesses Daniel's God 'a God of gods and a Lord of kings' — the superlative-of-superlatives sovereignty formula behind 'Lord of lords, and King of kings.' Hays: distinctive collocation. Theodotion Dan 2:47.

echoes.text: Give thanks to the Lord of lords; for his loving kindness endures forever:
echoes.note: 'Give thanks to the Lord of lords' — liturgical source reinforcing the 'Lord of lords' title applied to the Lamb. Hays: distinctive title, lower volume than Deut 10:17. LXX Ps 135:3.

echoes.text: I saw, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them;
echoes.note: The horn 'made war with the saints and prevailed' — the kings/beast who 'war against the Lamb' invert this; here the Lamb overcomes. Hays: thematic coherence, reversal of Daniel's beast-victory.

echoes.text: Through his policy he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand; and he shall magnify himself in his heart, and he shall destroy many in their security. He shall also stand up against the prince of princes; but he shall be broken without hand.
echoes.note: The king who 'stands up against the Prince of princes' but is 'broken without hand' parallels the kings warring on the Lamb and being overcome. Faint, structural. Hays: low.

echoes.text: The kings of the earth take a stand, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahweh, and against his Anointed, saying,
echoes.note: 'The kings of the earth set themselves... against the LORD and his Anointed' — the assembled kings making war on the Messiah/Lamb. Faint background; Ps 2 colors Rev broadly. Hays: coherence, low distinctiveness. LXX Ps 2:2.

echoes.text: The king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself, and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak marvelous things against the God of gods; and he shall prosper until the indignation be accomplished; for that which is determined shall be done.
echoes.note: The king who exalts himself above every god 'until the indignation is accomplished' parallels the beast-allied kings acting until God's purpose is done (cf. v.17). Faint. Hays: low.

pericopes.text: He said to me, “The waters which you saw, where the prostitute sits, are peoples, multitudes, nations, and languages. The ten horns which you saw, and the beast, these will hate the prostitute, and will make her desolate, and will make her naked, and will eat her flesh, and will burn her utterly with fire. For God has put in their hearts to do what he has in mind, and to be of one mind, and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God should be accomplished. The woman whom you saw is the great city, which reigns over the kings of the earth.”

echoes.text: You who dwell on many waters, abundant in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your covetousness.
echoes.note: Babylon 'who dwells on many waters' — the interpretive gloss 'the waters... are peoples, multitudes, nations, and languages' decodes the Jeremianic many-waters as the imperial multitude. Hays: recurrence (frames the unit with 17:1), distinctiveness. LXX Jer 28:13.

echoes.text: I will set my jealousy against you, and they shall deal with you in fury; they shall take away your nose and your ears; and your residue shall fall by the sword: they shall take your sons and your daughters; and your residue shall be devoured by the fire. They shall also strip you of your clothes, and take away your beautiful jewels. Thus will I make your lewdness to cease from you, and your prostitution from the land of Egypt; so that you shall not lift […]
echoes.note: Oholibah's former lovers, in fury, deal with her in hatred, 'strip you of your clothes,' leave you 'naked and bare,' and 'deal with you in hatred' — the precise source for the horns/beast who 'hate the prostitute,' 'make her desolate,' 'strip her naked,' and consume her. Hays: volume, distinctive hatred-and-stripping sequence.

echoes.text: therefore see, I will gather all your lovers, with whom you have taken pleasure, and all those who you have loved, with all those who you have hated; I will even gather them against you on every side, and will uncover your nakedness to them, that they may see all your nakedness. I will judge you, as women who break wedlock and shed blood are judged; and I will bring on you the blood of wrath and jealousy. I will also give you into their hand, and they […]
echoes.note: God gathers the harlot Jerusalem's lovers against her to 'strip you of your clothes,' leave you 'naked and bare,' stone you and 'burn your houses with fire' — parallel template for stripping naked and burning the harlot utterly with fire. Hays: distinctive strip-and-burn judgment of the harlot.

echoes.text: Make sharp the arrows; hold firm the shields: Yahweh has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes; because his purpose is against Babylon, to destroy it: for it is the vengeance of Yahweh, the vengeance of his temple.
echoes.note: 'The LORD has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, for his purpose is against Babylon to destroy it' — God moving foreign kings' spirits to execute judgment on Babylon is the source for 'God has put in their hearts' to give their kingdom to the beast until his words are fulfilled. Hays: distinctive divine-instigation-of-kings motif. LXX Jer 28:11.

echoes.text: now therefore, behold, the Lord brings upon them the mighty flood waters of the River: the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will come up over all its channels, and go over all its banks.
echoes.note: 'The waters of the River, strong and many — the king of Assyria and all his glory' explicitly equates floodwaters with imperial peoples/armies — the OT precedent for waters = peoples and nations. Hays: distinctive waters-as-nations equation. LXX Isa 8:7.

echoes.text: There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
echoes.note: 'All peoples, nations, and languages should serve him' — the stock Danielic fourfold (peoples/nations/languages) underlies 'peoples, multitudes, nations, and languages.' Hays: distinctive fourfold list, recurrence at Rev 5:9; 7:9; 13:7. Theodotion Dan 7:14.

echoes.text: Thus says Yahweh: Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and shall become an overflowing stream, and shall overflow the land and all that is therein, the city and those who dwell therein; and the men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall wail.
echoes.note: 'Waters rise out of the north and shall become an overflowing flood... it shall overflow the land and all that is in it' — invading nations imaged as overwhelming waters, supporting the waters = peoples decoding. Hays: thematic coherence. LXX Jer 29:2.

echoes.text: “‘The daughter of any priest, if she profanes herself by playing the prostitute, she profanes her father. She shall be burned with fire.
echoes.note: The priest's daughter who plays the harlot 'shall be burned with fire' — the Torah penalty of burning for cultic harlotry behind the harlot's burning with fire. Hays: distinctive harlot-burning statute. LXX Lev 21:9.

echoes.text: I will also give you into their hand, and they shall throw down your vaulted place, and break down your lofty places; and they shall strip you of your clothes, and take your beautiful jewels; and they shall leave you naked and bare. They shall also bring up a company against you, and they shall stone you with stones, and thrust you through with their swords.
echoes.note: The lovers 'shall break down your eminent place... shall leave you naked and bare' and the company 'shall stone you... and thrust you through with their swords' — reinforces the desolation-and-violence inflicted on the harlot-city by her own allies. Hays: coherence (companion to 16:37–41).

echoes.text: The king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself, and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak marvelous things against the God of gods; and he shall prosper until the indignation be accomplished; for that which is determined shall be done.
echoes.note: Events run 'until the indignation is accomplished, for that which is determined shall be done' — parallel to 'until the words of God should be accomplished.' Faint structural echo of decreed-end formula. Hays: low.

echoes.text: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “There is yet one man by whom we may inquire of Yahweh; but I hate him, for he never prophesies good concerning me, but always evil. He is Micaiah the son of Imla.” Jehoshaphat said, “Don’t let the king say so.”
echoes.note: Generic background to 'hate the prostitute' as kings turning against a former ally; very faint. Listed for maximal coverage. Hays: low.

pericopes.text: After these things, I saw another angel coming down out of the sky, having great authority. The earth was illuminated with his glory. He cried with a mighty voice, saying, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, and she has become a habitation of demons, a prison of every unclean spirit, and a prison of every unclean and hateful bird! For all the nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her sexual immorality, the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the abundance of her luxury.”

echoes.text: Behold, here comes a troop of men, horsemen in pairs.” He answered, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the engraved images of her gods are broken to the ground.
echoes.note: The double cry 'Fallen, fallen is Babylon' (peptōken, peptōken Babylōn) reproduces the watchman's announcement in Isaiah's oracle against Babylon almost verbatim (LXX Isa 21:9 'peptōken Babylōn'). Hays: volume and recurrence very high; Revelation doubles the verb for emphasis. The single most secure base text for v.2.

echoes.text: Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed: wail for her; take balm for her pain, if so be she may be healed.
echoes.note: 'Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed' (LXX Jer 28:8) reinforces the Isaianic cry; the conflation of Isa 21:9 + Jer 50-51 is characteristic of John's oracular technique. Thematic and verbal volume high; satisfies Hays availability and recurrence (Jeremiah's Babylon oracle pervades the chapter).

echoes.text: Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldeans’ pride, will be like when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. It will never be inhabited, neither will it be lived in from generation to generation. The Arabian will not pitch a tent there, neither will shepherds make their flocks lie down there. But wild animals of the desert will lie there, and their houses will be full of jackals. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will frolic there. […]
echoes.note: Babylon's fall leaving her a haunt of wild creatures and unclean beasts (jackals, ostriches, satyrs/demons dancing in her ruins) supplies 'habitation of demons... unclean and hateful bird.' LXX Isa 13:21 has daimonia dancing there. Strong figural and lexical correspondence (LXX 'daimonia').

echoes.text: But the pelican and the porcupine will possess it. The owl and the raven will dwell in it. He will stretch the line of confusion over it, and the plumb line of emptiness. They shall call its nobles to the kingdom, but none shall be there; and all its princes shall be nothing. Thorns will come up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in its fortresses; and it will be a habitation of jackals, a court for ostriches. The wild animals of the desert will meet […]
echoes.note: Oracle against Edom: the desolate land becomes a dwelling of unclean birds (owl, raven, jackal, wild beasts, and night-creatures/Lilith) 'forever.' Supplies the 'haunt of every unclean bird' imagery transferred to Babylon. Hays: dissimilarity and thematic coherence strong; combined with Isa 13.

echoes.text: Therefore the wild animals of the desert with the wolves shall dwell there, and the ostriches shall dwell therein: and it shall be no more inhabited forever; neither shall it be lived in from generation to generation.
echoes.note: 'Wild beasts of the desert with hyenas shall dwell there, and ostriches... no more inhabited forever' (LXX Jer 27:39). Direct prophetic source for Babylon as permanent haunt of unclean creatures and demons.

echoes.text: Babylon shall become heaps, a dwelling place for jackals, an astonishment, and a hissing, without inhabitant.
echoes.note: 'Babylon shall become heaps, a dwelling place for jackals, a horror and a hissing, without inhabitant' (LXX Jer 28:37). Reinforces the 'habitation of demons'/desolation theme; recurrence within Jeremiah's Babylon oracle high.

echoes.text: Babylon has been a golden cup in Yahweh’s hand, who made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunk of her wine; therefore the nations are mad.
echoes.note: 'Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand, making all the earth drunken; the nations have drunk of her wine, therefore the nations are mad' (LXX Jer 28:7). Direct source for 'all the nations have drunk of the wine of... her' — the intoxication-of-nations motif. Strong verbal and thematic volume.

echoes.text: For thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, to me: take this cup of the wine of wrath at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send you, to drink it. They shall drink, and reel back and forth, and be mad, because of the sword that I will send among them. Then took I the cup at Yahweh’s hand, and made all the nations to drink, to whom Yahweh had sent me: Jerusalem, and the cities of Judah, and its kings, and its princes, to make them a desolation, an […]
echoes.note: The cup of the wine of wrath made to drink by all the nations (vv.15-16, 27) underlies the fused 'wine of the wrath' phrase. Revelation blends the cup-of-wrath (Jer 25) with Babylon's own intoxicating cup (Jer 51:7); coherence good, but mediated.

echoes.text: It will happen after the end of seventy years that Yahweh will visit Tyre, and she shall return to her wages, and will play the prostitute with all the kingdoms of the world on the surface of the earth.
echoes.note: Tyre as the harlot who 'plays the harlot with all the kingdoms of the world' and whose merchandise is gain — supplies the kings/merchants committing immorality and growing rich. Tyre-typology stands behind v.3 alongside Babylon. Hays: thematic coherence; mediated through the merchant-lament structure.

echoes.text: because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft.
echoes.note: Nineveh 'the well-favored harlot, the mistress of sorceries, who sells nations through her whoredom' — the harlot-city seducing nations parallels Babylon's fornication with the kings (cf. also v.23 sorcery). Figural correspondence; contested as direct source.

echoes.text: When your wares went out of the seas, you filled many peoples; you enriched the kings of the earth with the multitude of your riches and of your merchandise.
echoes.note: Tyre 'enriched the kings of the earth with the multitude of your riches and merchandise' — anticipates 'merchants of the earth grew rich from her luxury.' Fuller resonance appears in the merchant lament (18:11-19); faint here.

pericopes.text: I heard another voice from heaven, saying, “Come out of her, my people, that you have no participation in her sins, and that you don’t receive of her plagues, for her sins have reached to the sky, and God has remembered her iniquities. Return to her just as she returned, and repay her double as she did, and according to her works. In the cup which she mixed, mix to her double. However much she glorified herself, and grew wanton, so much give her of torment and mourning. For she says in her heart, ‘I sit a queen, and am no widow, and will in no way see mourning.’ Therefore in one day her plagues will come: death, mourning, and famine; and she will be utterly burned with fire; for the Lord God who has judged her is strong.

echoes.text: My people, go away from the midst of her, and save yourselves every man from the fierce anger of Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Come out of the midst of her, my people, and save yourselves each one from the fierce anger of the LORD' (LXX Jer 28:45). The summons 'Come out of her, my people' is near-verbatim and the strongest base text for v.4. Hays: volume and recurrence very high.

echoes.text: Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and save every man his life; don’t be cut off in her iniquity: for it is the time of Yahweh’s vengeance; he will render to her a recompense.
echoes.note: 'Flee out of the midst of Babylon... be not cut off in her iniquity' (LXX Jer 28:6) — parallel exodus-from-Babylon command tied to not sharing her punishment; reinforces v.4's 'that you don't receive of her plagues.' Doublet of 51:45.

echoes.text: Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans. With a voice of singing declare, tell this, utter it even to the end of the earth: say, Yahweh has redeemed his servant Jacob.
echoes.note: 'Go forth from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans' — the second-Isaiah exodus-from-Babylon summons. Combines with Jer 51 to form the 'come out' call. Strong thematic/lexical coherence.

echoes.text: Depart, depart, go out from there, touch no unclean thing! Go out of the midst of her! Cleanse yourselves, you who bear the vessels of Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Depart, depart, go out from there, touch no unclean thing; go out of the midst of her, be clean' — separation from defilement underlies 'have no participation in her sins.' (Also cited at 2 Cor 6:17.) Hays: recurrence in NT separation-paraenesis high.

echoes.text: Shout against her all around: she has submitted herself; her bulwarks are fallen, her walls are thrown down; for it is the vengeance of Yahweh: take vengeance on her; as she has done, do to her.
echoes.note: 'Take vengeance on her; as she has done, do to her' (LXX Jer 27:15) — the lex talionis 'render to her as she rendered' of v.6. Strong verbal match for the requital formula.

echoes.text: Call together the archers against Babylon, all those who bend the bow; encamp against her all around; let none of it escape: recompense her according to her work; according to all that she has done, do to her; for she has been proud against Yahweh, against the Holy One of Israel.
echoes.note: 'Recompense her according to her work; according to all that she has done, do to her' (LXX Jer 27:29). Parallel requital command, reinforcing 'according to her works' and 'repay double as she did.'

echoes.text: Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, he will be happy who rewards you, as you have served us.
echoes.note: 'O daughter of Babylon... happy shall he be who repays you as you have served us' (LXX Ps 136:8). The 'repay/render to Babylon' motif; the doubling ('repay her double') extends the lex talionis. Coherence high; the only Psalter source in the chapter.

echoes.text: “Speak comfortably to Jerusalem; and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of Yahweh’s hand double for all her sins.”
echoes.note: Jerusalem 'received from the LORD's hand double for all her sins' — the 'double' (diplous) language is inverted: Babylon now drinks the double. Verbal contact on 'double'; figural reversal. Hays: dissimilarity makes the allusion plausible though contested.

echoes.text: First I will recompense their iniquity and their sin double, because they have polluted my land with the carcasses of their detestable things, and have filled my inheritance with their abominations.
echoes.note: 'I will recompense their iniquity and their sin double' — Jeremianic source for repaying 'double' (diplous, LXX). Supports the doubling formula in v.6 alongside the requital commands.

echoes.text: You said, ‘I shall be a mistress forever;’ so that you did not lay these things to your heart, nor did you remember the latter end of it. “Now therefore hear this, you who are given to pleasures, who sit securely, who say in your heart, ‘I am, and there is no one else besides me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children:’ but these two things shall come to you in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood; in […]
echoes.note: Virgin daughter Babylon: 'I shall be a mistress/queen forever... I shall not sit as a widow nor know loss of children' (LXX Isa 47:7-8) and 'these two things shall come in one day, loss of children and widowhood' (47:9). Direct source for both 'I sit a queen, am no widow' (v.7) AND 'in one day her plagues' (v.8). Very strong, multi-point match.

echoes.text: This is the joyous city that lived carelessly, that said in her heart, “I am, and there is no one besides me.” How she has become a desolation, a place for animals to lie down in! Everyone who passes by her will hiss, and shake their fists.
echoes.note: Nineveh: 'the exultant city that dwelt securely, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none besides me.' The self-secure boast 'in her heart' parallels Babylon's 'she says in her heart, I sit a queen.' Verbal/thematic correspondence strong.

echoes.text: They said, “Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make ourselves a name, lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole earth.”
echoes.note: Babel building a tower 'with its top in the heavens' faintly stands behind 'her sins have reached to the sky' (v.5); the Babel-Babylon hubris reaching heaven. Faint, contested figural link.

echoes.text: We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed: forsake her, and let us go everyone into his own country; for her judgment reaches to heaven, and is lifted up even to the skies.
echoes.note: 'Her judgment reaches to heaven and is lifted up to the skies' (LXX Jer 28:9) — closer source than Babel for 'her sins have reached to the sky' (v.5). Verbal match on judgment/sin reaching heaven.

echoes.text: Then Yahweh rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from Yahweh out of the sky. He overthrew those cities, all the plain, all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew on the ground. But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt. Abraham got up early in the morning to the place where he had stood before Yahweh. He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward all the land of the plain, and looked, and saw that […]
echoes.note: Sodom 'burned with fire' and its rising smoke (cf. v.9 smoke of her burning) tints 'utterly burned with fire.' The destroyed-city-by-fire archetype; faint, mediated.

echoes.text: and say, Thus says the Lord Yahweh: Behold, I am against you, Sidon; and I will be glorified in your midst; and they shall know that I am Yahweh, when I shall have executed judgments in her, and shall be sanctified in her.
echoes.note: Judgment on a proud city/prince that exalts itself, vindicating God 'when I have executed judgments... and am sanctified' — coheres with 'the Lord God who has judged her is strong.' Faint thematic echo.

pericopes.text: The kings of the earth, who committed sexual immorality and lived wantonly with her, will weep and wail over her, when they look at the smoke of her burning, standing far away for the fear of her torment, saying, ‘Woe, woe, the great city, Babylon, the strong city! For your judgment has come in one hour.’

echoes.text: Then all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, and lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments: they shall clothe themselves with trembling; they shall sit on the ground, and shall tremble every moment, and be astonished at you. They shall take up a lamentation over you, and tell you, How you are destroyed, who were inhabited by seafaring men, the renowned city, who was strong in the sea, she and her inhabitants, […]
echoes.note: The princes of the sea descend from their thrones, clothe themselves in trembling, sit on the ground appalled at Tyre, and take up a lamentation: 'How you have perished!' The kings standing in fear and raising the lament over the fallen city derives directly from this Tyre dirge. Strong structural and thematic source.

echoes.text: and shall cause their voice to be heard over you, and shall cry bitterly, and shall cast up dust on their heads, they shall wallow themselves in the ashes: and they shall make themselves bald for you, and clothe them with sackcloth, and they shall weep for you in bitterness of soul with bitter mourning. In their wailing they shall take up a lamentation for you, and lament over you, saying, Who is there like Tyre, like her who is brought to silence in the […]
echoes.note: Mariners and pilots 'cry bitterly... take up a lamentation over you and wail over you... What city is like Tyre?' The weeping-and-wailing-over-the-burning-city pattern (recurring in vv.11,18-19) is built on Ezek 27's Tyre lament. High volume across the three laments.

echoes.text: Now shall the islands tremble in the day of your fall; yes, the islands that are in the sea shall be dismayed at your departure.
echoes.note: 'Now shall the isles tremble in the day of your fall' — the trembling/fear at the moment of the city's fall underlies 'standing far away for the fear of her torment.' Reinforces the Tyre-dirge framing.

echoes.text: At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth trembles, and the cry is heard among the nations.
echoes.note: 'At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth trembles, and the cry is heard among the nations' (LXX Jer 27:46) — the nations' reaction to Babylon's specific fall. Coheres with kings wailing over Babylon; mediated by the Tyre template.

echoes.text: Wail; for the day of Yahweh is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty. Therefore all hands will be feeble, and everyone’s heart will melt. They will be dismayed. Pangs and sorrows will seize them. They will be in pain like a woman in labor. They will look in amazement one at another. Their faces will be faces of flame.
echoes.note: 'Wail, for the day of the LORD is near... they shall be amazed... pangs shall take hold of them' in the Babylon oracle — the lament/anguish at Babylon's day faintly informs the kings' wailing. Faint, contested.

echoes.text: Its streams will be turned into pitch, its dust into sulfur, And its land will become burning pitch. It won’t be quenched night nor day. Its smoke will go up forever. From generation to generation, it will lie waste. No one will pass through it forever and ever.
echoes.note: Edom's land becomes burning pitch, 'its smoke shall go up forever' — supplies the 'smoke of her burning' motif (also vv.18; cf. Gen 19:28). Faint verbal contact on rising smoke of judgment.

pericopes.text: The merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, for no one buys their merchandise any more; merchandise of gold, silver, precious stones, pearls, fine linen, purple, silk, scarlet, all expensive wood, every vessel of ivory, every vessel made of most precious wood, and of brass, and iron, and marble; and cinnamon, incense, perfume, frankincense, wine, olive oil, fine flour, wheat, sheep, horses, chariots, and people’s bodies and souls. The fruits which your soul lusted after have been lost to you, and all things that were dainty and sumptuous have perished from you, and you will find them no more at all. The merchants of these things, who were made rich by her, will stand far away for the fear of her torment, weeping and mourning; saying, ‘Woe, woe, the great city, she who was dressed in fine linen, purple, and scarlet, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls! For in an hour such great riches are made desolate.’ Every ship master, and everyone who sails anywhere, and mariners, and as many as gain their living by sea, stood far away, and cried out as they looked at the smoke of her burning, saying, ‘What is like the great city?’ They cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and mourning, saying, ‘Woe, woe, the great city, in which all who had their ships in the sea were made rich by reason of her great wealth!’ For in one hour is she made desolate.

echoes.text: Tarshish was your merchant by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches; with silver, iron, tin, and lead, they traded for your wares. Javan, Tubal, and Meshech, they were your traffickers; they traded the persons of men and vessels of brass for your merchandise. They of the house of Togarmah traded for your wares with horses and war horses and mules. The men of Dedan were your traffickers; many islands were the market of your hand: they brought you […]
echoes.note: The extended cargo manifest of Tyre's trading partners (silver, iron, tin, lead, ivory, ebony, purple, fine linen, precious stones, gold, spices, wine, wheat, oil, horses, slaves [27:13 'the souls of men'], etc.) is the direct quarry for Revelation's merchandise list (vv.12-13). Many items match item-for-item. The single most important source for the pericope; volume and recurrence very high.

echoes.text: Your riches, and your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, and your pilots, your repairers of ship seams, and the dealers in your merchandise, and all your men of war, who are in you, with all your company which is in your midst, shall fall into the heart of the seas in the day of your ruin.
echoes.note: 'Your riches, your wares, your merchandise, your mariners and pilots... all your company shall fall into the heart of the seas in the day of your ruin' — the loss of all wealth 'in one hour... made desolate' echoes Tyre's total commercial ruin. Strong thematic and lexical link.

echoes.text: All who handled the oar, the mariners, and all the pilots of the sea, shall come down from their ships; they shall stand on the land, and shall cause their voice to be heard over you, and shall cry bitterly, and shall cast up dust on their heads, they shall wallow themselves in the ashes: and they shall make themselves bald for you, and clothe them with sackcloth, and they shall weep for you in bitterness of soul with bitter mourning. In their wailing […]
echoes.note: Shipmasters, mariners, and all who handle the sea come down from their ships, stand on the land, cry bitterly, cast dust on their heads, wallow in ashes, and lament 'What city is like Tyre?' Direct source for the sailors' lament (vv.17-19): 'Every ship master... stood far away,' 'cast dust on their heads,' 'What is like the great city?' Near point-by-point correspondence; highest-confidence sub-source.

echoes.text: Then all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, and lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments: they shall clothe themselves with trembling; they shall sit on the ground, and shall tremble every moment, and be astonished at you.
echoes.note: The sea-princes 'clothe themselves with trembling, sit on the ground, tremble... and are astonished at you' — supplies the merchants/sailors standing afar in fear and mourning. Reinforces Ezek 27 across vv.15-19.

echoes.text: When your wares went out of the seas, you filled many peoples; you enriched the kings of the earth with the multitude of your riches and of your merchandise.
echoes.note: 'By your great wealth and merchandise you enriched the kings of the earth' — direct source for 'all who had their ships in the sea were made rich by reason of her great wealth' (v.19) and 'merchants... made rich by her' (v.15). Verbal match on enriching by merchandise.

echoes.text: The merchants among the peoples hiss at you; you are become a terror, and you shall nevermore have any being.
echoes.note: 'The merchants among the peoples hiss at you; you have become a terror and shall be no more forever' — the merchants' reaction and the city's vanishing; coheres with 'you will find them no more' and the merchants' dismay. Closely tied to the Tyre dirge.

echoes.text: The burden of Tyre. Howl, you ships of Tarshish! For it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in. From the land of Kittim it is revealed to them. Be still, you inhabitants of the coast, you whom the merchants of Sidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished. On great waters, the seed of the Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue. She was the market of nations. Be ashamed, Sidon; for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the […]
echoes.note: The oracle against Tyre, the trading city of the nations, whose merchants are princes (cf. 23:8 'whose merchants are the honored of the earth') — Tyre-as-marketplace stands behind the merchant lament and 'your merchants were the princes' (18:23). Wail of the ships of Tarshish (23:1,14) parallels the sailors' lament. Hays: thematic coherence high; mediated alongside Ezek 27.

echoes.text: and they shall make themselves bald for you, and clothe them with sackcloth, and they shall weep for you in bitterness of soul with bitter mourning.
echoes.note: 'They shall make themselves bald for you, gird with sackcloth, and weep over you with bitterness of soul' — reinforces 'weeping and mourning' and the casting of dust/mourning rites (v.19). Part of the Ezek 27 lament cluster.

echoes.text: All that pass by clap their hands at you. They hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, Is this the city that men called The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?
echoes.note: Passersby clap, hiss, and ask of fallen Jerusalem 'Is this the city...?' — the astonished 'What is like the great city?' rhetorical question is a recognized mourning-formula; faint, more directly from Ezek 27:32.

echoes.text: Joshua tore his clothes, and fell to the earth on his face before Yahweh’s ark until the evening, he and the elders of Israel; and they put dust on their heads.
echoes.note: Casting dust on the head as a gesture of grief/lament (cf. also 1 Sam 4:12; Job 2:12; Lam 2:10) is a stock mourning rite informing v.19; the proximate source is Ezek 27:30. Background convention, not specific allusion.

echoes.text: You were in Eden, the garden of God; every precious stone adorned you: ruby, topaz, emerald, chrysolite, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and beryl. Gold work of tambourines and of pipes was in you. In the day that you were created they were prepared.
echoes.note: The list of precious stones and gold adorning the king of Tyre in Eden faintly colors Babylon 'decked with gold and precious stones and pearls' (v.16). Faint, mediated by the broader Tyre cycle.

pericopes.text: “Rejoice over her, O heaven, you saints, apostles, and prophets; for God has judged your judgment on her.” A mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone and cast it into the sea, saying, “Thus with violence will Babylon, the great city, be thrown down, and will be found no more at all. The voice of harpists, minstrels, flute players, and trumpeters will be heard no more at all in you. No craftsman, of whatever craft, will be found any more at all in you. The sound of a mill will be heard no more at all in you. The light of a lamp will shine no more at all in you. The voice of the bridegroom and of the bride will be heard no more at all in you; for your merchants were the princes of the earth; for with your sorcery all the nations were deceived. In her was found the blood of prophets and of saints, and of all who have been slain on the earth.”

echoes.text: It shall be, when you have made an end of reading this book, that you shall bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of the Euphrates: and you shall say, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise again because of the evil that I will bring on her; and they shall be weary. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.
echoes.note: Seraiah is told to bind a stone to the scroll and cast it into the Euphrates, saying 'Thus shall Babylon sink, to rise no more' (LXX Jer 28:63-64). Direct source for the angel casting the millstone into the sea: 'Thus with violence will Babylon be thrown down, and will be found no more.' The sign-act and the 'sink, no more' formula match closely. Highest-confidence source for v.21.

echoes.text: Moreover I will take from them the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp.
echoes.note: 'I will banish from them the voice of mirth and gladness, the voice of bridegroom and bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp' (LXX Jer 25:10/32:10). Direct, multi-item source for vv.22-23: millstone, lamp, bridegroom and bride all cease. Verbatim cluster; very high volume.

echoes.text: I will cause the noise of your songs to cease; and the sound of your harps shall be no more heard.
echoes.note: 'I will cause the noise of your songs to cease, and the sound of your harps shall be heard no more' — direct source for 'the voice of harpists... will be heard no more in you' (v.22). Tyre-dirge silencing of music. Strong verbal match.

echoes.text: I will make you a terror, and you shall no more have any being; though you are sought for, yet you will never be found again, says the Lord Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'I will make you a terror, and you shall be no more; though you be sought, you shall never be found again' (LXX Ezek 26:21). Direct source for 'will be found no more at all' (v.21) — the never-to-be-found-again finality applied to Babylon. High confidence.

echoes.text: Then the heavens and the earth, and all that is therein, shall sing for joy over Babylon; for the destroyers shall come to her from the north, says Yahweh. As Babylon has caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the land.
echoes.note: 'Babylon must fall for the slain of Israel, as the slain of all the earth have fallen for Babylon' (LXX Jer 28:49). Direct source for v.24 'in her was found the blood... of all who have been slain on the earth.' Heaven and earth rejoice (51:48) parallels 'Rejoice over her, O heaven' (v.20). Strong dual link.

echoes.text: Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and save every man his life; don’t be cut off in her iniquity: for it is the time of Yahweh’s vengeance; he will render to her a recompense. Babylon has been a golden cup in Yahweh’s hand, who made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunk of her wine; therefore the nations are mad.
echoes.note: Babylon's sorcery/intoxication corrupting the nations (cf. 51:7 nations 'mad') underlies 'with your sorcery all the nations were deceived' (v.23). Verbal/thematic recurrence within the Jeremiah Babylon oracle.

echoes.text: because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft.
echoes.note: Nineveh 'the mistress of sorceries, who sells nations through her whoredom and families through her sorceries' — direct source for 'with your sorcery (pharmakeia) all the nations were deceived' (v.23). The harlot-city + sorcery + deceiving nations cluster matches closely.

echoes.text: Who has planned this against Tyre, the giver of crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honorable of the earth?
echoes.note: Tyre 'whose merchants are princes, whose traders are the honored of the earth' — direct source for 'your merchants were the princes of the earth' (v.23). Verbal correspondence on merchants-as-princes.

echoes.text: Then I will cause to cease from the cities of Judah, and from the streets of Jerusalem, the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; for the land shall become a waste.”
echoes.note: 'I will cause to cease... the voice of mirth and gladness, the voice of bridegroom and bride; for the land shall become desolate' — doublet of Jer 25:10 reinforcing the silenced bridegroom/bride of v.23 (cf. also Jer 16:9; 33:11). Recurrent prophetic desolation-formula.

echoes.text: Rejoice, you nations, with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his servants. He will take vengeance on his adversaries, and will make atonement for his land and for his people.
echoes.note: 'Rejoice, O nations/heavens, with his people, for he avenges the blood of his servants' (LXX/4QDeut expanded) — the call for heaven to rejoice because God avenges his servants' blood parallels v.20 + v.24 (blood of prophets and saints avenged). Hays: thematic coherence; the vengeance-of-blood frame.

echoes.text: Yahweh said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries to me from the ground.
echoes.note: Abel's blood crying from the ground — the foundational 'blood found/avenged' motif behind 'in her was found the blood' of all the slain (v.24). Faint archetypal echo; proximate source is Jer 51:49.

echoes.text: Also the blood of the souls of the innocent poor is found in your skirts. You did not find them breaking in; but it is because of all these things.
echoes.note: 'On your skirts is found the lifeblood of the innocent poor' — the idiom of a city in which innocent blood 'is found' resonates with v.24's 'in her was found the blood.' Faint verbal contact on blood being 'found.'

pericopes.text: After these things I heard something like a loud voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying, “Hallelujah! Salvation, power, and glory belong to our God: for true and righteous are his judgments. For he has judged the great prostitute, who corrupted the earth with her sexual immorality, and he has avenged the blood of his servants at her hand.” A second said, “Hallelujah! Her smoke goes up forever and ever.” The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sits on the throne, saying, “Amen! Hallelujah!” A voice came from the throne, saying, “Give praise to our God, all you his servants, you who fear him, the small and the great!”

echoes.text: Let sinners be consumed out of the earth. Let the wicked be no more. Bless Yahweh, my soul. Praise Yah!
echoes.note: First of four 'Hallelujah!' acclamations in Rev 19, the only occurrences in the NT. The Hebrew 'Halleluyah' (LXX Allelouia) closes Ps 104 (LXX 103) at the destruction of sinners from the earth - thematically exact to the destruction of the prostitute. Volume/recurrence strong.

echoes.text: Praise Yahweh! Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.
echoes.note: Ps 106 (LXX 105) opens with 'Halleluyah' joined to praise of God's salvation and judgment; the Egyptian Hallel cluster (Pss 104-106, 111-118, 135, 146-150) is the matrix John draws on. Recurrence + thematic coherence.

echoes.text: Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting! Let all the people say, “Amen.” Praise Yah!
echoes.note: Doxological close of Book IV of the Psalter: 'Blessed be the LORD... Amen. Hallelujah.' Exactly mirrors Rev 19:4's 'Amen! Hallelujah!' from the elders/living creatures. LXX Allelouia + Amen pairing is the precise verbal seam.

echoes.text: Praise Yah! Praise, you servants of Yahweh, praise Yahweh’s name.
echoes.note: Opening of the Hallel proper, 'Halleluyah! Praise, O servants of the LORD' - matches the throne-voice summons to 'all you his servants' (Rev 19:5). LXX Allelouia + douloi.

echoes.text: Praise Yah! Praise Yahweh’s name! Praise him, you servants of Yahweh,
echoes.note: 'Hallelujah! Praise the name of the LORD; praise him, O servants of the LORD' - the 'praise our God, all his servants' summons of Rev 19:5 stands closest to this Hallel verse. LXX Ps 134:1.

echoes.text: He will bless those who fear Yahweh, both small and great.
echoes.note: 'He will bless those who fear the LORD, both small and great.' The pairing 'fear him, the small and the great' in Rev 19:5 reproduces this collocation (mikros kai megas). LXX Ps 113:21.

echoes.text: House of Levi, praise Yahweh! You who fear Yahweh, praise Yahweh!
echoes.note: 'You who fear the LORD, bless the LORD' - reinforces the 'you who fear him' clause; faint, one of several Hallel parallels.

echoes.text: Rejoice, you nations, with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his servants. He will take vengeance on his adversaries, and will make atonement for his land and for his people.
echoes.note: Song of Moses: God 'avenges the blood of his servants' and 'renders vengeance to his adversaries' - the verbatim conceptual source of 'he has avenged the blood of his servants at her hand' (Rev 19:2). LXX expands with heavenly rejoicing, strengthening the link; cf. Rev 6:10. Volume + thematic coherence very high.

echoes.text: You shall strike the house of Ahab your master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of Yahweh, at the hand of Jezebel.
echoes.note: Jezebel the prototype prostitute-queen: 'that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets... at the hand of Jezebel.' The phrase 'avenge the blood of my servants at the hand of' is reproduced almost exactly, mapping Babylon/the prostitute onto Jezebel (cf. Rev 2:20). Strong verbal recurrence.

echoes.text: The Rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are just. A God of faithfulness who does no wrong, just and right is he.
echoes.note: 'all his ways are justice... just and right is he' undergirds 'true and righteous are his judgments' (Rev 19:2). Song-of-Moses framing reinforced by the v.43 vengeance link.

echoes.text: The fear of Yahweh is clean, enduring forever. Yahweh’s ordinances are true, and righteous altogether.
echoes.note: 'the judgments of the LORD are true and righteous altogether' (LXX Ps 18:10 ta krimata kyriou alethina, dedikaiomena) is the closest verbal donor for 'true and righteous are his judgments' (Rev 19:2). LXX wording near-quotation.

echoes.text: You are righteous, Yahweh. Your judgments are upright.
echoes.note: 'Righteous are you, O LORD, and upright are your judgments' - alternate Psalmic donor for the true/righteous-judgments formula; faint.

echoes.text: Its streams will be turned into pitch, its dust into sulfur, And its land will become burning pitch. It won’t be quenched night nor day. Its smoke will go up forever. From generation to generation, it will lie waste. No one will pass through it forever and ever.
echoes.note: Oracle against Edom: the land's 'smoke shall go up forever; from generation to generation it shall lie waste' - the direct source of 'Her smoke goes up forever and ever' (Rev 19:3). Combined with the Sodom/Gomorrah burning topos (Gen 19:28). Verbal volume high.

echoes.text: He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward all the land of the plain, and looked, and saw that the smoke of the land went up as the smoke of a furnace.
echoes.note: Smoke of Sodom 'going up like the smoke of a furnace' - the foundational rising-smoke-of-judgment image behind Rev 19:3, reinforcing Isa 34. Babylon = anti-city judged like Sodom.

echoes.text: For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is prepared. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.
echoes.note: Topheth's burning pyre with the LORD's breath kindling it; contributes to the eternal-smoke imagery. Faint.

echoes.text: Then the heavens and the earth, and all that is therein, shall sing for joy over Babylon; for the destroyers shall come to her from the north, says Yahweh.
echoes.note: Heaven and earth and all in them sing for joy over Babylon's fall - background for heaven's rejoicing/Hallelujah over the prostitute Babylon; thematic not verbal.

echoes.text: All her streets will say, “Hallelujah!” and give praise, saying, “Blessed be God, who has exalted you forever!”
echoes.note: Second-Temple: Tobit's hymn over the restored Jerusalem ends 'and all her lanes will say Hallelujah and give praise' (cf. 13:11 nations gathering). Closest Second-Temple precedent for liturgical Hallelujah tied to a city's vindication; contrast with fallen Babylon. Flag as Greek-tradition parallel.

echoes.text: Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting. All the people said, “Amen,” and praised Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Blessed be the LORD... Amen and praise the LORD' (the Asaph doxology quoting Ps 106:48) - reinforces the 'Amen! Hallelujah!' seam of Rev 19:4. Derivative of Ps 106:48.

echoes.text: before Yahweh; for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, the peoples with his truth.
echoes.note: 'he comes to judge the earth; he will judge the world with righteousness' supports the righteous-judgment theme of vv.1-2; faint here, primary in the rider pericope.

pericopes.text: I heard something like the voice of a great multitude, and like the voice of many waters, and like the voice of mighty thunders, saying, “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God, the Almighty, reigns! Let us rejoice and be exceedingly glad, and let us give the glory to him. For the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his wife has made herself ready.” It was given to her that she would array herself in bright, pure, fine linen: for the fine linen is the righteous acts of the saints. He said to me, “Write, ‘Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.’” He said to me, “These are true words of God.” I fell down before his feet to worship him. He said to me, “Look! Don’t do it! I am a fellow bondservant with you and with your brothers who hold the testimony of Jesus. Worship God, for the testimony of Jesus is the Spirit of Prophecy.”

echoes.text: When they went, I heard the noise of their wings like the noise of great waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a noise of tumult like the noise of an army: when they stood, they let down their wings.
echoes.note: The living creatures' wings 'like the sound of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty' - direct source of 'the voice of many waters' AND its conjunction with 'the Almighty' (pantokrator) in Rev 19:6. Verbal volume + Ezekiel throne-vision context very strong.

echoes.text: Behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like the sound of many waters; and the earth shined with his glory.
echoes.note: The glory of God returning to the temple, 'his voice was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone with his glory.' Doublet with 1:24 reinforcing the 'many waters' theophanic acclamation of Rev 19:6. LXX phone hydaton pollon.

echoes.text: his body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches, and his arms and his feet like burnished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
echoes.note: The man clothed in linen has 'the sound of his words like the noise of a multitude' - contributes the multitude-voice element; chief donor in the rider pericope but resonant here.

echoes.text: Yahweh reigns! Let the earth rejoice! Let the multitude of islands be glad!
echoes.note: 'The LORD reigns; let the earth rejoice' (LXX 96:1, ho kyrios ebasileusen) - the enthronement-psalm shout behind 'the Lord our God, the Almighty, reigns!' joined to 'let us rejoice' (Rev 19:6-7). Cf. Pss 93:1; 96:10; 99:1.

echoes.text: Yahweh reigns! He is clothed with majesty! Yahweh is armed with strength. The world also is established. It can’t be moved.
echoes.note: 'The LORD reigns, he is clothed with majesty' (LXX 92:1) - one of the YHWH-malak enthronement psalms underlying the 'reigns!' acclamation; cluster reference with Pss 96-99.

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: 'I will greatly rejoice in the LORD... he has clothed me with garments of salvation... as a bridegroom decks himself... and as a bride adorns herself' - the source of bridal self-adornment ('his wife has made herself ready') joined to rejoicing (Rev 19:7-8). Verbal + thematic coherence high.

echoes.text: For as a young man marries a virgin, so your sons shall marry you; and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
echoes.note: 'as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you' - Zion-as-bride marriage imagery feeding the Lamb's marriage; reinforces Isa 61:10.

echoes.text: For your Maker is your husband; Yahweh of Armies is his name: and the Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer; the God of the whole earth shall he be called. For Yahweh has called you as a wife forsaken and grieved in spirit, even a wife of youth, when she is cast off,” says your God.
echoes.note: 'your Maker is your husband... the LORD has called you like a wife forsaken' - covenantal husband-wife template behind the marriage of the Lamb to his bride/wife (Rev 19:7).

echoes.text: I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion. I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'I will betroth you to me forever... in righteousness and justice' - betrothal in righteousness undergirds the bride's 'righteous acts' linen and the marriage motif; contrast with the unfaithful prostitute just judged. Thematic coherence.

echoes.text: In this mountain, Yahweh of Armies will make all peoples a feast of fat things, a feast of choice wines, of fat things full of marrow, of well refined choice wines.
echoes.note: The eschatological feast on Zion: 'the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food' - the OT matrix for 'the marriage supper of the Lamb' (Rev 19:9), the messianic banquet. Thematic source par excellence.

echoes.text: to appoint to those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.
echoes.note: 'garment of praise' / 'oaks of righteousness' contributes to the righteousness-as-garment idea of v.8; faint, subsidiary to 61:10.

echoes.text: The princess inside is all glorious. Her clothing is interwoven with gold. She shall be led to the king in embroidered work. The virgins, her companions who follow her, shall be brought to you.
echoes.note: Royal wedding psalm: the king's bride 'in many-colored robes... led to the king' - the royal-bridal-array image behind the linen-clad wife of the Lamb (Rev 19:7-8). LXX Ps 44.

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
echoes.note: Beatitude/blessing formula and end-time deliverance background for 'Blessed are those invited' (Rev 19:9); faint beatitude resonance.

echoes.text: Blessed is he who waits, and comes to the one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
