echoes.note: 'Blessed is he who waits' - Danielic macarism pattern behind the Apocalypse's beatitudes (cf. Rev 19:9, one of seven). Faint.

pericopes.text: I saw the heaven opened, and behold, a white horse, and he who sat on it is called Faithful and True. In righteousness he judges and makes war. His eyes are a flame of fire, and on his head are many crowns. He has names written and a name written which no one knows but he himself. He is clothed in a garment sprinkled with blood. His name is called “The Word of God.”

echoes.text: His delight will be in the fear of Yahweh. He will not judge by the sight of his eyes, neither decide by the hearing of his ears; but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked. Righteousness will be the belt of his waist, and faithfulness the belt of his waist.
echoes.note: The messianic shoot 'with righteousness he shall judge the poor... righteousness shall be the belt of his waist' - the source of 'in righteousness he judges and makes war' (Rev 19:11). Combined with 11:4 (slaying the wicked with the breath/rod of his mouth, central to the next pericope). Verbal + Davidic-messiah coherence high.

echoes.text: before Yahweh; for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, the peoples with his truth.
echoes.note: 'he comes to judge the earth; he will judge the world in righteousness' (LXX 95:13, krinei... en dikaiosyne) - the closest verbal donor for 'in righteousness he judges' (Rev 19:11). Cf. Ps 98:9.

echoes.text: Let them sing before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity.
echoes.note: 'he will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity' (LXX 97:9) - doublet of 96:13 reinforcing the righteous-judgment formula of v.11.

echoes.text: his body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches, and his arms and his feet like burnished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
echoes.note: The man clothed in linen: 'his eyes like flaming torches' (LXX hosei lampades pyros) - direct source of 'his eyes are a flame of fire' (Rev 19:12; cf. 1:14; 2:18). Verbal volume high.

echoes.text: I saw until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
echoes.note: The Ancient of Days' throne 'a fiery flame' and the divine fire-imagery support the flame-of-fire eyes; Danielic theophanic register fused into the rider.

echoes.text: Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this who is glorious in his clothing, marching in the greatness of his strength? “It is I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save.” Why are you red in your clothing, and your garments like him who treads in the wine vat? “I have trodden the wine press alone; and of the peoples there was no man with me: yes, I trod them in my anger, and trampled them in my wrath; and their lifeblood is […]
echoes.note: The divine warrior from Edom 'crimsoned garments... red... like one who treads the winepress... their blood spattered on my garments' - direct source of the blood-sprinkled garment (Rev 19:13), here pre-battle (his own blood / enemies' anticipated). Verbal volume high; primary in the next pericope's winepress too.

echoes.text: It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.
echoes.note: The root of Jesse as a 'signal' / standard, supporting the named-and-known messianic rider; faint, secondary to 11:3-5.

echoes.text: The nations shall see your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of Yahweh shall name.
echoes.note: 'you shall be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give' - background for 'a name written which no one knows but he himself' (Rev 19:12); the hidden/new divine-given name motif. Cf. Rev 2:17; 3:12.

echoes.text: You shall leave your name for a curse to my chosen; and the Lord Yahweh will kill you; and he will call his servants by another name:
echoes.note: 'the Lord GOD will... call his servants by another name' - reinforces the new/secret-name theme of v.12; faint.

echoes.text: Your all-powerful word leaped from heaven out of the royal throne, A stern warrior, into the midst of the doomed land, Bearing as a sharp sword your unfeigned commandment; And standing it filled all things with death; And while it touched the heaven it trode upon the earth.
echoes.note: Second-Temple: God's 'all-powerful word leaped from heaven... a stern warrior carrying the sharp sword of your authentic command' striking the land. The closest Jewish precedent personifying the divine Word as warrior - background for 'His name is called The Word of God' (Rev 19:13) joined to the sword of v.15. Flag as Greek-tradition parallel.

echoes.text: Binding his foal to the vine, his donkey’s colt to the choice vine; he has washed his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
echoes.note: Judah 'washed his garments in wine and his robe in the blood of grapes' - messianic Judah oracle blending wine/blood/garment; possible faint donor to the blood-stained robe and winepress complex.

echoes.text: Now in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth of the month, as I was among the captives by the river Chebar, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
echoes.note: 'the heavens were opened and I saw visions of God' - the opened-heaven inaugural formula behind 'I saw the heaven opened' (Rev 19:11); cf. Ezek 1:1 LXX. Faint, conventional.

pericopes.text: The armies which are in heaven followed him on white horses, clothed in white, pure, fine linen. Out of his mouth proceeds a sharp, double-edged sword, that with it he should strike the nations. He will rule them with an iron rod. He treads the wine press of the fierceness of the wrath of God, the Almighty. He has on his garment and on his thigh a name written, “KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.”

echoes.text: but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.
echoes.note: 'he shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked' - direct source of the sword 'out of his mouth' to 'strike the nations' (Rev 19:15). The LXX renders 'with the word of his mouth' (to logo tou stomatos), tightening the link to 'The Word of God' (v.13). Verbal volume + LXX coherence very high.

echoes.text: You shall break them with a rod of iron. You shall dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.”
echoes.note: 'You shall break them with a rod of iron' - direct source of 'He will rule them with an iron rod' (Rev 19:15; cf. 2:27; 12:5). The MT reads 'break' (te-ro'em), the LXX 'shepherd/rule' (poimaneis); Rev follows the LXX 'rule/shepherd.' Flag MT-vs-LXX: John uses LXX poimaino.

echoes.text: Why are you red in your clothing, and your garments like him who treads in the wine vat? “I have trodden the wine press alone; and of the peoples there was no man with me: yes, I trod them in my anger, and trampled them in my wrath; and their lifeblood is sprinkled on my garments, and I have stained all my clothing. For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redeemed has come. I looked, and there was no one to help; and I wondered that […]
echoes.note: 'I have trodden the winepress alone... I trampled them in my anger... their lifeblood spattered... for the day of vengeance was in my heart' - direct source of 'He treads the wine press of the fierceness of the wrath of God' (Rev 19:15). Verbal volume high; pairs with the blood-stained robe of v.13.

echoes.text: Put in the sickle; for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the wine press is full, the vats overflow, for their wickedness is great.”
echoes.note: 'Put in the sickle... the winepress is full, the vats overflow, for their wickedness is great' (LXX 4:13) - the eschatological winepress-of-judgment image fused with Isa 63 in 'treads the wine press of... wrath' (Rev 19:15; cf. 14:19-20). Verbal + thematic.

echoes.text: The Lord has set at nothing all my mighty men in the midst of me; He has called a solemn assembly against me to crush my young men: The Lord has trodden as in a wine press the virgin daughter of Judah.
echoes.note: 'the Lord has trodden as in a winepress the virgin daughter of Judah' - additional winepress-trampling donor; faint, subsidiary to Isa 63 / Joel 3.

echoes.text: The king answered to Daniel, and said, Of a truth your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.
echoes.note: Nebuchadnezzar to Daniel: 'your God is God of gods and Lord of kings' (LXX theos ton theon kai kyrios ton basileon) - principal Danielic source for the divine title 'KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS' (Rev 19:16; cf. 17:14). Verbal coherence high.

echoes.text: For Yahweh your God, he is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the awesome, who doesn’t respect persons, nor takes reward.
echoes.note: 'the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords' (LXX theos ton theon kai kyrios ton kyrion) - the foundational 'Lord of lords' title, near-verbatim source for Rev 19:16. Verbal volume high.

echoes.text: Give thanks to the Lord of lords; for his loving kindness endures forever:
echoes.note: 'Give thanks to the Lord of lords' (LXX 135:3 to kyrio ton kyrion) - liturgical donor for 'Lord of lords' in Rev 19:16; cf. Deut 10:17. Hallel-context reinforces the chapter's Hallelujah frame.

echoes.text: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and extol and honor the King of heaven; for all his works are truth, and his ways justice; and those who walk in pride he is able to abase.
echoes.note: Nebuchadnezzar's doxology to the 'King of heaven' - reinforces the King-of-kings supreme-sovereign register; faint, subsidiary to Dan 2:47.

echoes.text: and he has made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand, he has hidden me: and he has made me a polished shaft; in his quiver has he kept me close:
echoes.note: The Servant: 'he made my mouth like a sharp sword' - donor for the sharp sword proceeding from the mouth (Rev 19:15; cf. 1:16). Complements Isa 11:4.

echoes.text: I will make my arrows drunk with blood. My sword shall devour flesh with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the head of the leaders of the enemy.”
echoes.note: Song of Moses: 'I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh' - the divine sword devouring flesh links to the warrior's sword and the carnage of vv.17-21; faint here.

pericopes.text: I saw an angel standing in the sun. He cried with a loud voice, saying to all the birds that fly in the sky, “Come! Be gathered together to the great supper of God, that you may eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of captains, the flesh of mighty men, and the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them, and the flesh of all men, both free and slave, and small and great.” I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him who sat on the horse, and against his army. The beast was taken, and with him the false prophet who worked the signs in his sight, with which he deceived those who had received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped his image. These two were thrown alive into the lake of fire that burns with sulfur. The rest were killed with the sword of him who sat on the horse, the sword which came out of his mouth. All the birds were filled with their flesh.

echoes.text: You, son of man, thus says the Lord Yahweh: Speak to the birds of every sort, and to every animal of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel, that you may eat flesh and drink blood. You shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, of lambs, and of goats, of bulls, all of them […]
echoes.note: The Gog oracle's sacrificial feast: 'Speak to the birds of every sort... assemble... to the sacrificial feast that I am preparing for you... you shall eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of the princes... horses and riders, mighty men and all the men of war.' Direct, sustained source of the angel summoning the birds to 'the great supper of God' to eat the flesh of kings, captains, mighty men, horses and riders (Rev 19:17-18). Verbal volume + structural parallel very high; inverts the marriage supper of v.9.

echoes.text: Be silent at the presence of the Lord Yahweh, for the day of Yahweh is at hand. For Yahweh has prepared a sacrifice. He has consecrated his guests.
echoes.note: 'the LORD has prepared a sacrifice and consecrated his guests' for the day of the LORD - the sacrificial-feast-of-judgment motif behind 'the great supper of God' (Rev 19:17), feeding into the Ezek 39 banquet.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s sword is filled with blood. It is covered with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams; for Yahweh has a sacrifice in Bozrah, And a great slaughter in the land of Edom. The wild oxen will come down with them, and the young bulls with the mighty bulls; and their land will be drunken with blood, and their dust made greasy with fat.
echoes.note: The LORD's sword 'filled with blood... gorged with fat' and a great slaughter/sacrifice in Edom; the gory sword-sacrifice imagery reinforces the carnage and the devouring-flesh supper of vv.17-21. Same Edom oracle as the smoke of 19:3.

echoes.text: but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.
echoes.note: Slaying the wicked with the breath/word of his mouth - the sword 'which came out of his mouth' kills 'the rest' (Rev 19:21), recapitulating 19:15 and its Isa 11:4 source.

echoes.text: I saw at that time because of the voice of the great words which the horn spoke; I saw even until the animal was slain, and its body destroyed, and it was given to be burned with fire.
echoes.note: 'the beast was killed, and its body destroyed and given over to be burned with fire' - direct source of the beast taken and cast into the lake of fire (Rev 19:20). Danielic fourth-beast destruction; verbal + structural coherence high.

echoes.text: For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is prepared. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.
echoes.note: Topheth prepared, 'a pyre of fire and wood... the breath of the LORD, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it' - the fire-and-sulfur (theion) lake into which the beast and false prophet are thrown (Rev 19:20). LXX theion link.

echoes.text: Then Yahweh rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from Yahweh out of the sky.
echoes.note: The LORD rained 'sulfur and fire' on Sodom - foundational sulfur-and-fire judgment image behind 'the lake of fire that burns with sulfur' (Rev 19:20).

echoes.text: and whoever doesn’t fall down and worship shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.
echoes.note: The fiery furnace for those refusing to worship the image inverts the beast's image-worship; faint conceptual contrast (image-worship -> fire) with the lake of fire and the worshipers of the image.

echoes.text: The kings of the earth take a stand, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahweh, and against his Anointed, saying,
echoes.note: 'The kings of the earth set themselves... against the LORD and against his anointed' - direct source of 'the kings of the earth and their armies gathered together to make war against him who sat on the horse' (Rev 19:19). Continues the Ps 2 frame (cf. iron rod, v.15).

echoes.text: I will call for a sword against him to all my mountains, says the Lord Yahweh: every man’s sword shall be against his brother. With pestilence and with blood will I enter into judgment with him; and I will rain on him, and on his hordes, and on the many peoples who are with him, an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, fire, and sulfur.
echoes.note: Gog's hordes destroyed: 'every man's sword against his brother... fire and sulfur' rained on Gog - the assembled armies, sword-slaughter, and fire/sulfur of vv.19-21 draw on the wider Gog war, alongside Ezek 39's bird-feast.

echoes.text: Proclaim this among the nations: “Prepare for war! Stir up the mighty men. Let all the warriors draw near. Let them come up. Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, ‘I am strong.’ Hurry and come, all you surrounding nations, and gather yourselves together.” Cause your mighty ones to come down there, Yahweh. “Let the nations arouse themselves, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat; for there will I sit to […]
echoes.note: 'Gather all the nations... let them come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge' - the gathering of the nations/kings for the eschatological battle and judgment (Rev 19:19); pairs with the Joel 3:13 winepress of v.15.

echoes.text: I will make my arrows drunk with blood. My sword shall devour flesh with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the head of the leaders of the enemy.”
echoes.note: 'my sword shall devour flesh' (Song of Moses) - the devouring sword and the birds gorged on flesh recapitulate this; faint, also flagged at 19:15.

pericopes.text: I saw an angel coming down out of heaven, having the key of the abyss and a great chain in his hand. He seized the dragon, the old serpent, which is the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole inhabited earth, and bound him for a thousand years, and cast him into the abyss, and shut it, and sealed it over him, that he should deceive the nations no more, until the thousand years were finished. After this, he must be freed for a short time.

echoes.text: It shall happen in that day that Yahweh will punish the army of the high ones on high, and the kings of the earth on the earth. They shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison; and after many days shall they be visited.
echoes.note: The clearest structural model: YHWH punishes 'the host of the high ones' / the kings of the earth, who are 'gathered together as prisoners in the pit, and shut up in the prison; and after many days shall they be visited.' Hays volume/recurrence: imprisonment of hostile powers, sealing in the pit, then a later release/visitation maps onto bound-for-a-thousand-years then 'freed for a short time.' LXX uses synagōgē/desmōtērion imagery; Hebrew 'bor' (pit) parallels the abyss.

echoes.text: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which Yahweh God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden?’”
echoes.note: 'the old serpent' (ho ophis ho archaios) draws the Eden serpent into the dragon's identity; recurrence with Rev 12:9. The serpent of Gen 3 is the deceiver-archetype, matching 'who deceives the whole inhabited earth.' Verbal echo via LXX ophis.

echoes.text: God created the large sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, after their kind, and every winged bird after its kind. God saw that it was good.
echoes.note: tannin/dragon (LXX ta kētē) as primeval sea-monster contributes to the 'dragon' image, though Rev's dragon is more directly the chaos-monster of the prophets than the created sea creatures.

echoes.text: In that day, Yahweh with his hard and great and strong sword will punish leviathan, the fleeing serpent, and leviathan the twisted serpent; and he will kill the dragon that is in the sea.
echoes.note: YHWH 'shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent... and he shall slay the dragon (LXX drakonta) that is in the sea.' The dragon/serpent chaos-beast slain or subdued; 'serpent' + 'dragon' pairing parallels Rev 20:2's stacked epithets. Hays satisfaction: same eschatological defeat of the chaos-serpent.

echoes.text: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
echoes.note: 'Am I a sea, or a whale (tannin/dragon), that you set a watch over me?' — God setting a guard over the sea-monster; faint background to the chaining/sealing of the dragon.

echoes.text: A stone was brought, and laid on the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.
echoes.note: The stone laid on the lions' den 'sealed (LXX esphragisato) with the king's own signet... that the purpose might not be changed' — verbal/conceptual parallel to shutting and sealing over the abyss so the dragon cannot escape. Faint, contested.

echoes.text: Yet you shall be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.
echoes.note: The rebel power 'brought down to Sheol, to the sides of the pit' — the casting-down-into-the-pit of a deceiving heavenly power resonates with casting Satan into the abyss.

pericopes.text: I saw thrones, and they sat on them, and judgment was given to them. I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, and for the word of God, and such as didn’t worship the beast nor his image, and didn’t receive the mark on their forehead and on their hand. They lived, and reigned with Christ for a thousand years. The rest of the dead didn’t live until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection. Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection. Over these, the second death has no power, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with him one thousand years.

echoes.text: I saw until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
echoes.note: 'I beheld till the thrones were cast down (set up)' (LXX/Theod. ethrēsan heōs hou hoi thronoi etethēsan) — the plural 'thrones' set for judgment is the direct verbal source for 'I saw thrones.' Hays volume: distinctive plural thrones in a judgment vision.

echoes.text: until the ancient of days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the Most High, and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom.
echoes.note: 'judgment was given to the saints of the most High' (Theod. krima edōken hagiois) — exact source of 'judgment was given to them.' The saints share the divine tribunal; recurrence with Dan 7:27.

echoes.text: The kingdom and the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole sky, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High: his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.
echoes.note: 'the kingdom... shall be given to the people of the saints' — the saints' reign/kingship undergirds 'they lived and reigned with Christ.' Coherent with the thrones-and-judgment cluster from Dan 7.

echoes.text: and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.”
echoes.note: 'ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests' (LXX basileion hierateuma) — direct source of 'priests of God... and will reign.' Recurrence with Rev 1:6 and 5:10. Royal-priesthood of the redeemed people.

echoes.text: But you shall be named the priests of Yahweh; men will call you the ministers of our God: you will eat the wealth of the nations, and you will boast in their glory.
echoes.note: 'ye shall be named the Priests of the LORD' (LXX hiereis kyriou klēthēsesthe) — the eschatological people as priests of God; reinforces Exod 19:6 for 'priests of God and of Christ.'

echoes.text: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
echoes.note: 'many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame' — the source for resurrection-to-life vs. the second death and for distinguishing 'the first resurrection' from the rest. Hays thematic coherence with the two-outcome resurrection.

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
echoes.note: 'everyone that shall be found written in the book' delivered — the blessing on those who 'have part in the first resurrection' echoes the deliverance of the book-enrolled at the resurrection; coheres with the book-of-life motif resolved in 20:12,15.

echoes.text: But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.
echoes.note: 'the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever' — the everlasting reign of the saints parallels reigning with Christ; part of the Dan 7 throne complex.

echoes.text: But you shall be named the priests of Yahweh; men will call you the ministers of our God: you will eat the wealth of the nations, and you will boast in their glory.
echoes.note: (continuation) 'ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles' — broader Isa 61 priest-people-vindicated background to the martyrs' reversal of the beast's persecution; the vindication of those who refused the mark.

echoes.text: So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up on their feet, an exceedingly great army.
echoes.note: The slain in the vision 'lived, and stood up' (LXX ezēsan) — the resurrection-vivification verb 'they lived' (ezēsan) may echo the Ezekiel dry-bones revival; faint lexical parallel.

pericopes.text: And after the thousand years, Satan will be released from his prison, and he will come out to deceive the nations which are in the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to the war; the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. They went up over the breadth of the earth, and surrounded the camp of the saints, and the beloved city. Fire came down out of heaven from God, and devoured them. The devil who deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet are also. They will be tormented day and night forever and ever.

echoes.text: Son of man, set your face toward Gog, of the land of Magog, the prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal, and prophesy against him,
echoes.note: 'set thy face against Gog, the land of Magog' — the proper names 'Gog and Magog' are lifted directly from Ezekiel; Rev makes Magog a second figure rather than a land, but the verbal source is unmistakable. Hays volume/recurrence: explicit naming.

echoes.text: You shall come from your place out of the uttermost parts of the north, you, and many peoples with you, all of them riding on horses, a great company and a mighty army; and you shall come up against my people Israel, as a cloud to cover the land: it shall happen in the latter days, that I will bring you against my land, that the nations may know me, when I shall be sanctified in you, Gog, before their eyes.
echoes.note: Gog comes 'out of the north... a great company, and a mighty army... thou shalt come up against my people of Israel, as a cloud to cover the land' — source for the gathered host marching up against God's people. Coheres with 'went up over the width of the earth... surrounded the camp.'

echoes.text: With pestilence and with blood will I enter into judgment with him; and I will rain on him, and on his hordes, and on the many peoples who are with him, an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, fire, and sulfur.
echoes.note: 'I will rain upon him... fire and brimstone' (LXX pyr kai theion) — direct source of 'fire came down out of heaven... and devoured them' and of 'lake of fire and sulfur.' Strong lexical match (pyr/theion).

echoes.text: I will send a fire on Magog, and on those who dwell securely in the islands; and they shall know that I am Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'I will send a fire on Magog' — reinforces the fire-from-God consuming Gog/Magog; recurrence with 38:22. Direct thematic and onomastic link.

echoes.text: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your seed greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your seed will possess the gate of his enemies.
echoes.note: 'as the sand which is upon the sea shore' (LXX hōs hē ammos hē para to cheilos tēs thalassēs) — innumerable-as-the-sand idiom for the gathered army. Also Josh 11:4; 1 Sam 13:5 use it of hostile hosts; Hays: stock biblical idiom for countless multitude.

echoes.text: and I will turn you around, and will lead you on, and will cause you to come up from the uttermost parts of the north; and I will bring you on the mountains of Israel; and I will strike your bow out of your left hand, and will cause your arrows to fall out of your right hand. You shall fall on the mountains of Israel, you, and all your hordes, and the peoples who are with you: I will give you to the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the animals of the […]
echoes.note: Gog brought 'upon the mountains of Israel' and destroyed there — the host's advance onto the holy land/people parallels surrounding the camp of the saints and the beloved city.

echoes.text: For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city will be taken, the houses rifled, and the women ravished. Half of the city will go out into captivity, and the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.
echoes.note: 'I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle' — the eschatological gathering of the nations to war against the holy city undergirds 'gather them together to the war' and 'the beloved city.' Hays coherence with the Zech siege motif.

echoes.text: “Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of reeling to all the surrounding peoples, and on Judah also will it be in the siege against Jerusalem. It will happen in that day, that I will make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all the peoples. All who burden themselves with it will be severely wounded, and all the nations of the earth will be gathered together against it.
echoes.note: Jerusalem made 'a cup of trembling' and 'a burdensome stone' against which 'all the people of the earth be gathered' — siege of the city by all nations, then their destruction; parallels the surrounding-then-consumed pattern.

echoes.text: Elijah answered to the captain of fifty, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from the sky, and consume you and your fifty!” Fire came down from the sky, and consumed him and his fifty.
echoes.note: 'let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee' (LXX katabēsetai pyr ek tou ouranou) — closest lexical parallel for 'fire came down out of heaven... and devoured them'; Hays volume on the exact phrase though the Ezek 38–39 context is primary.

echoes.text: Yahweh loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
echoes.note: 'The LORD loveth the gates of Zion' — possible background to 'the beloved city' (tēn polin tēn ēgapēmenēn) as the city God loves; faint, the epithet may be Rev's own coinage.

echoes.text: For, behold, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, that march through the breadth of the earth, to possess dwelling places that are not theirs.
echoes.note: The invader who 'march[es] through the breadth of the land' (LXX poreuomenon epi ta platē tēs gēs) — close lexical parallel to 'went up over the width of the earth (epi to platos tēs gēs).'

echoes.text: For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is prepared. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.
echoes.note: Topheth prepared, 'the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone (theion), doth kindle it' — source for the fiery lake of burning/brimstone into which the devil is thrown; provides the burning-pile-of-fire-and-brimstone image.

echoes.text: “They shall go out, and look on the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they will be loathsome to all mankind.”
echoes.note: 'their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched' — the unending torment of the condemned ('tormented day and night forever and ever') resonates with the unquenchable fire of Isaiah's final verse.

echoes.text: I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by him who lives forever that it shall be for a time, times, and a half; and when they have made an end of breaking in pieces the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.
echoes.note: Oath 'by him that liveth for ever' (eis ton aiōna) — the 'forever and ever' eternity formula has Danielic resonance, though it is a stock LXX/Rev liturgical phrase.

pericopes.text: I saw a great white throne, and him who sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away. There was found no place for them. I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne, and they opened books. Another book was opened, which is the book of life. The dead were judged out of the things which were written in the books, according to their works. The sea gave up the dead who were in it. Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them. They were judged, each one according to his works. Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire. If anyone was not found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire.

echoes.text: A fiery stream issued and came out from before him: thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
echoes.note: 'the judgment was set, and the books were opened' (LXX/Theod. kritērion ekathisen, kai bibloi ēneōchthēsan) — direct source for 'they opened books' and judgment before the throne. Hays volume: the opened-books-of-judgment is distinctively Danielic.

echoes.text: I saw until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
echoes.note: 'his throne was like the fiery flame... the Ancient of days did sit' — the enthroned judge whose throne dominates the scene; source for 'a great white throne, and him who sat on it.' Whiteness draws on the Ancient of Days' garment 'white as snow.'

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book. Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
echoes.note: 'every one that shall be found written in the book' delivered, and the dead 'awake... some to everlasting life, and some to... everlasting contempt' — the book-enrollment determining destiny and the resurrection-to-judgment of all the dead. Source for the book of life deciding the lake of fire.

echoes.text: Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken in pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors; and the wind carried them away, so that no place was found for them: and the stone that struck the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
echoes.note: The smashed image elements blown away 'and no place was found for them' (LXX kai topos ouch heurethē autois) — near-verbatim source of 'There was found no place for them' (topos ouch heurethē autois). Strong lexical match.

echoes.text: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, and not be written with the righteous.
echoes.note: 'Let them be blotted out of the book of the living (LXX biblou zōntōn)... not be written with the righteous' — the book of life from which names are absent; source for being judged by enrollment / 'not found written in the book of life.'

echoes.text: Yet now, if you will, forgive their sin—and if not, please blot me out of your book which you have written.” Yahweh said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.
echoes.note: 'blot me out of thy book which thou hast written... whosoever hath sinned... will I blot out of my book' — the divine register of the living/saved; foundational for the book-of-life motif alongside Ps 69:28.

echoes.text: I, Yahweh, search the mind, I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.
echoes.note: 'I the LORD search the heart... to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings' — direct source of the recurring 'judged... according to their works / according to his works.' Hays recurrence with Ps 62:12; Rev 2:23; 22:12.

echoes.text: Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.
echoes.note: 'thou renderest to every man according to his work' (LXX kata ta erga autou) — closest lexical parallel to 'each one according to his works'; reinforces Jer 17:10 as the judged-by-works topos.

echoes.text: “Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will recompense, yes, I will recompense into their bosom,
echoes.note: 'it is written before me... I will recompense, even recompense into their bosom' — the written record before God grounding judgment by deeds; parallels the books of works opened in judgment.

echoes.text: The sea saw it, and fled. The Jordan was driven back.
echoes.note: 'The sea saw it, and fled' (LXX hē thalassa... ephygen) — the fleeing of sea/earth before God; lexical resonance with earth and heaven that 'fled away' (ephygen) from the throne. Hays: theophanic flight of creation.

echoes.text: Tremble, you earth, at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Jacob,
echoes.note: 'Tremble, thou earth, at the presence of the Lord' — creation's terrified retreat before God's face; coheres with earth/heaven fleeing from his face.

echoes.text: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol. I will redeem them from death! Death, where are your plagues? Sheol, where is your destruction? “Compassion will be hidden from my eyes.
echoes.note: 'I will ransom them from the power of the grave (Sheol/Hades); I will redeem them from death: O death... O grave (LXX hadē), I will be thy destruction' — source for Death and Hades surrendering the dead and then being destroyed (thrown into the lake of fire). Hays: the personified Death/Hades pairing.

echoes.text: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.
echoes.note: 'He will swallow up death in victory' (LXX katepien ho thanatos ischysas) — the abolition of Death itself; source for Death being thrown into the lake of fire / the second death. Coheres with 1 Cor 15:54-55.

echoes.text: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
echoes.note: 'shame and everlasting contempt' for the resurrected wicked — the 'second death' as the negative resurrection outcome; reinforces the two-destiny judgment of all the dead.

echoes.text: Your dead shall live. My dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.
echoes.note: 'the earth shall cast out the dead (LXX hē gē tōn asebōn peseitai / dead shall arise)' — resurrection of the dead from the earth; faint background to land/sea/Hades giving up their dead.

echoes.text: [source text not in the World English Bible]
echoes.note: 'the earth shall give back that which has been entrusted to it, and Sheol... shall give back that which it owes' — Second-Temple parallel to 'the sea gave up the dead... Death and Hades gave up the dead.' Strong conceptual match for the universal resurrection-disgorging of the realms of the dead.

echoes.text: [source text not in the World English Bible]
echoes.note: Sheol/the chambers of souls restoring the dead at the consummation — Second-Temple background to the realms of the dead releasing their dead for judgment.

pericopes.text: I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and the sea is no more. I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband. I heard a loud voice out of heaven saying, “Behold, God’s dwelling is with people, and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God. He will wipe away from them every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain, any more. The first things have passed away.”

echoes.text: “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.
echoes.note: Verbal and thematic core: 'new heavens and a new earth' (LXX ouranos kainos kai ge kaine) with the 'former things not remembered/passed away' motif — John's 'new heaven and a new earth' and 'the first things have passed away' (v.4) draws on both halves. Strongest availability and recurrence; Hays' volume and thematic coherence both high.

echoes.text: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me,” says Yahweh, “so your seed and your name shall remain.
echoes.note: Doublet of 65:17: 'the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me' — reinforces the eschatological permanence theme. Together with 65:17 establishes the dominant intertext.

echoes.text: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.
echoes.note: 'He will wipe away every tear' (v.4) echoes 'the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces' and 'he will swallow up death forever' — joint source for tear-wiping and death's abolition. MT 'swallow up death' vs LXX 'death prevailed having swallowed' diverges; John follows the death-abolished sense (cf. MT / Theodotion). High volume.

echoes.text: My tent also shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
echoes.note: Covenant-dwelling formula: 'My dwelling place (LXX kataskenosis) will be with them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people' — directly behind v.3 ('God's dwelling is with people... they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God'). Recurrence with Lev 26 strengthens.

echoes.text: I will set my tent among you, and my soul won’t abhor you. I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.
echoes.note: Foundational covenant formula: 'I will set my tabernacle/dwelling among you... I will walk among you and be your God, and you shall be my people.' Source of the Ezek 37:27 reuse; Revelation's plural 'peoples' (laoi, best text) universalizes the singular covenant 'people.'

echoes.text: Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion; for, behold, I come, and I will dwell in your midst,’ says Yahweh. Many nations shall join themselves to Yahweh in that day, and shall be my people; and I will dwell in your midst, and you shall know that Yahweh of Armies has sent me to you.
echoes.note: 'I will dwell in the midst of you... and many nations shall join themselves to the LORD... and shall be my people' — supports v.3's expanded 'peoples' and the God-dwelling-with-humanity theme; verbal contact with the dwelling formula.

echoes.text: Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion; put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean.
echoes.note: 'Awake, awake... O Jerusalem, the holy city; put on your beautiful garments' — behind the 'holy city' title (v.2) and the adornment imagery; recurs at 21:27 ('nothing unclean shall enter').

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: Bridal-adornment simile (v.2): 'as a bridegroom decks himself... and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels' — close conceptual and verbal match for 'prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.'

echoes.text: For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her righteousness go out as brightness, and her salvation as a lamp that burns. The nations shall see your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of Yahweh shall name. You shall also be a crown of beauty in the hand of Yahweh, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God. You shall no more be termed Forsaken; […]
echoes.note: Zion as bride married to God: 'as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride... so shall your God rejoice over you'; the city given a new name. Supports the New Jerusalem-as-bride identification.

echoes.text: The Yahweh’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”
echoes.note: 'Sorrow and sighing shall flee away' parallels 'no more mourning, nor crying, nor pain' (v.4); paired with 51:11. Thematic coherence high though verbal contact diffuse.

echoes.text: The ransomed of Yahweh shall return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy shall be on their heads. They shall obtain gladness and joy. Sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
echoes.note: Doublet of 35:10 ('sorrow and sighing shall flee away'); reinforces the abolition-of-grief catalogue in v.4.

echoes.text: and I will bring them, and they will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they will be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.”
echoes.note: 'They shall be my people and I will be their God' — another instance of the covenant formula feeding v.3; faint given many parallel attestations.

echoes.text: I will sow her to me in the earth; and I will have mercy on her who had not obtained mercy; and I will tell those who were not my people, ‘You are my people;’ and they will say, ‘My God!’”
echoes.note: 'I will say... You are my people, and they shall say, You are my God' — covenant-formula reuse; low independent weight beside Lev 26 / Ezek 37.

echoes.text: There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
echoes.note: The 'peoples' (laoi) who serve in the everlasting kingdom may color the plural in v.3; faint and contested.

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
echoes.note: 'New heaven and a new earth' as deliberate recreation of the Gen 1 'heavens and the earth' — figural new-creation framing; structurally cued but verbally generic.

echoes.text: “Don’t remember the former things, and don’t consider the things of old.
echoes.note: 'Remember not the former things' — paired with 43:19 (next pericope); supports 'the first/former things have passed away' (v.4).

echoes.text: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
echoes.note: 'Am I the sea?' / the sea as chaos-monster domain may underlie 'the sea is no more' (v.1); part of the OT chaos-sea / Leviathan complex.

echoes.text: Daniel spoke and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the sky broke out on the great sea. Four great animals came up from the sea, diverse one from another.
echoes.note: The 'great sea' from which the beasts arise — 'the sea is no more' (v.1) as the elimination of the source of chaos/the beast (cf. Rev 13:1). Figural; contested.

pericopes.text: He who sits on the throne said, “Behold, I am making all things new.” He said, “Write, for these words of God are faithful and true.” He said to me, “It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End. I will give freely to him who is thirsty from the spring of the water of life. He who overcomes, I will give him these things. I will be his God, and he will be my son. But for the cowardly, unbelieving, sinners, abominable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers,idolaters, and all liars, their part is in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur, which is the second death.”

echoes.text: Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
echoes.note: 'Behold, I am making all things new' (v.5) draws on 'Behold, I am doing a new thing' (idou ego poio kaina, LXX) — the 'behold... new' formula. High verbal contact with the LXX of Isa 43:19.

echoes.text: “Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
echoes.note: 'I will give freely (dorean) to him who is thirsty from the spring of the water of life' (v.6) echoes 'Ho, every one who thirsts, come to the waters... without money' — free gift to the thirsty. Verbal ('thirsty,' 'freely/without price') and thematic match.

echoes.text: This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.
echoes.note: 'I am the first, and I am the last' underlies 'the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End' (v.6); recurs at Rev 1:8,17; 22:13. Cf. also Isa 41:4; 48:12 for the same self-predication.

echoes.text: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men;
echoes.note: 'I will be his father, and he shall be my son' — Davidic adoption formula directly behind 'I will be his God, and he will be my son' (v.7). Revelation democratizes the royal promise to every overcomer.

echoes.text: He will call to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and the rock of my salvation!’ I will also appoint him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
echoes.note: Davidic sonship: 'He shall cry to me, You are my Father, my God... I will make him the firstborn' — reinforces 2 Sam 7:14 behind v.7; royal-firstborn coloring.

echoes.text: “Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.
echoes.note: 'I am the first, I also am the last' — doublet of 44:6 supporting the Alpha-Omega self-designation (v.6).

echoes.text: It will happen in that day, that living waters will go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea; in summer and in winter will it be.
echoes.note: 'Living waters shall flow out from Jerusalem' supports 'the spring of the water of life' (v.6); fully developed in Rev 22:1. Thematic coherence high.

echoes.text: For with you is the spring of life. In your light shall we see light.
echoes.note: 'With you is the fountain of life' — direct verbal source for 'the spring of the water of life' (v.6); pege zoes in LXX.

echoes.text: “For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living waters, and cut them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
echoes.note: 'The fountain of living waters' (God) contrasted with broken cisterns — colors the 'spring of the water of life' (v.6).

echoes.text: They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun strike them: for he who has mercy on them will lead them, even by springs of water he will guide them.
echoes.note: 'Springs of water will guide them' for the redeemed who 'will not hunger or thirst' — feeds the thirst/spring motif (v.6); also echoed in Rev 7:16-17.

echoes.text: Then Yahweh rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from Yahweh out of the sky.
echoes.note: 'Fire and sulfur (brimstone)' raining on Sodom (v.8 'fire and sulfur') — the canonical brimstone-judgment image. Cf. Ezek 38:22; Ps 11:6.

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
echoes.note: 'Everyone whose name is written in the book' — undergirds the overcomer/inheritance contrast with the excluded (v.7-8) and the book-of-life of v.27.

echoes.text: With pestilence and with blood will I enter into judgment with him; and I will rain on him, and on his hordes, and on the many peoples who are with him, an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, fire, and sulfur.
echoes.note: 'Fire and sulfur' rained in judgment on Gog — reinforces the 'lake that burns with fire and sulfur' (v.8).

pericopes.text: One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls, who were loaded with the seven last plagues came, and he spoke with me, saying, “Come here. I will show you the wife, the Lamb’s bride.” He carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone, as if it were a jasper stone, clear as crystal; having a great and high wall; having twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels; and names written on them, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. On the east were three gates; and on the north three gates; and on the south three gates; and on the west three gates. The wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them twelve names of the twelve Apostles of the Lamb.

echoes.text: In the visions of God brought he me into the land of Israel, and set me down on a very high mountain, whereon was as it were the frame of a city on the south.
echoes.note: 'He carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city' (v.10) closely reproduces Ezekiel's visionary transport: 'he brought me... and set me upon a very high mountain, on which was the frame of a city.' Tour-of-the-city framework derives directly from Ezek 40-48.

echoes.text: These are the exits of the city: On the north side four thousand and five hundred reeds by measure; and the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel, three gates northward: the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one. At the east side four thousand and five hundred reeds, and three gates: even the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one. At the south side four thousand and […]
echoes.note: Twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes, three on each of the four sides (v.12-13), reproduces Ezekiel's gate-list (three N, three E, three S, three W, named for the tribes). Highest structural and verbal correspondence for the gates.

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: Bridal imagery resumed (v.9 'the wife, the Lamb's bride') — cf. 21:2; the bride 'adorned' theme carries into the jewel-glory description (v.11).

echoes.text: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory is risen on you. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you.
echoes.note: 'Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you' underlies 'having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone' (v.11). Isa 60 is the controlling intertext for the city's radiance and is quarried throughout 21:23-26.

echoes.text: Behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like the sound of many waters; and the earth shined with his glory. It was according to the appearance of the vision which I saw, even according to the vision that I saw when I came to destroy the city; and the visions were like the vision that I saw by the river Chebar; and I fell on my face. Yahweh’s glory came into the house by the way of the gate whose prospect is […]
echoes.note: 'The glory of the God of Israel... the earth shone with his glory' as it enters the temple-city — parallels the city 'having the glory of God' (v.11). Reinforces the Ezekielian glory-filling pattern.

echoes.text: “You afflicted, tossed with storms, and not comforted, behold, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires. I will make your pinnacles of rubies, and your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.
echoes.note: Jerusalem rebuilt with sapphires, jewels, and precious-stone gates — anticipates the jasper radiance (v.11) and is the chief source for the foundations/gates jewelry developed in 21:18-21.

echoes.text: The stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his name, they shall be for the twelve tribes.
echoes.note: The high priest's breastpiece bearing the names of the twelve tribes engraved on twelve stones (v.12 'names of the twelve tribes') — links the tribe-inscribed gates to priestly typology; develops fully at 21:19-20.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying, “The children of Israel shall encamp every man by his own standard, with the banners of their fathers’ houses: at a distance from the Tent of Meeting shall they encamp around it.” Those who encamp on the east side toward the sunrise shall be of the standard of the camp of Judah, according to their divisions: and the prince of the children of Judah shall be Nahshon the son of Amminadab. His division, and those […]
echoes.note: The wilderness camp arranged by tribes three-per-side around the tabernacle on the four compass points — pattern behind the three-gates-per-side arrangement (v.13).

echoes.text: Behold, a wall on the outside of the house all around, and in the man’s hand a measuring reed six cubits long, of a cubit and a hand breadth each: so he measured the thickness of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed.
echoes.note: The wall surrounding the temple-complex measured by the angel — anticipates the 'great and high wall' (v.12) and the measuring of 21:15-17.

pericopes.text: He who spoke with me had for a measure, a golden reed, to measure the city, its gates, and its walls. The city is square, and its length is as great as its breadth. He measured the city with the reed, Twelve thousand twelve stadia. Its length, breadth, and height are equal. Its wall is one hundred forty-four cubits, by the measure of a man, that is, of an angel. The construction of its wall was jasper. The city was pure gold, like pure glass. The foundations of the city’s wall were adorned with all kinds of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, chalcedony; the fourth, emerald; the fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, topaz; the tenth, chrysoprasus; the eleventh, jacinth; and the twelfth, amethyst. The twelve gates were twelve pearls. Each one of the gates was made of one pearl. The street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass.

echoes.text: He brought me there; and, behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate.
echoes.note: The angelic man with 'a measuring reed' who measures the temple-city (v.15 'a golden reed to measure the city') reproduces Ezekiel's measuring-tour guide. Recurs through Ezek 40-42.

echoes.text: These shall be its measures: the north side four thousand and five hundred, and the south side four thousand and five hundred, and on the east side four thousand and five hundred, and the west side four thousand and five hundred.
echoes.note: The holy district/city given equal square measurements on its four sides — source for 'the city is square, and its length is as great as its width' (v.16). Cf. Ezek 45:1-3 for the foursquare holy portion.

echoes.text: Within the oracle was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and twenty cubits in its height; and he overlaid it with pure gold: and he covered the altar with cedar.
echoes.note: The inner sanctuary (Holy of Holies) a perfect cube ('twenty cubits long, twenty wide, twenty high') overlaid with gold — behind 'its length, width, and height are equal' (v.16) and the all-gold city (v.18): the whole city is the Most Holy Place. Strong typological coherence.

echoes.text: “You afflicted, tossed with storms, and not comforted, behold, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires. I will make your pinnacles of rubies, and your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.
echoes.note: 'I will lay your foundations with sapphires... your gates of carbuncles, and all your border of precious stones' — the principal OT source for the jewel-adorned foundations and pearl-like gates (v.19-21). LXX of 54:12 has the gates of crystal/stones.

echoes.text: You shall set in it settings of stones, four rows of stones: a row of ruby, topaz, and beryl shall be the first row; and the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald; and the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; and the fourth row a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be enclosed in gold in their settings.
echoes.note: The twelve stones of the high priest's breastpiece (v.19-20 jewel list) — the foundations' twelve gems correspond to the priestly stones, though John's order/LXX equivalences differ. High volume; flag LXX (Exod 28:17-20 LXX) as John's likely stone-name source.

echoes.text: I lifted up my eyes, and saw, and behold, a man with a measuring line in his hand. Then I asked, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see what is its breadth and what is its length.”
echoes.note: The man with a measuring line going to measure Jerusalem — parallels the measuring of the city (v.15-16); paired with Ezek 40.

echoes.text: Moreover, when you shall divide by lot the land for inheritance, you shall offer an offering to Yahweh, a holy portion of the land; the length shall be the length of twenty-five thousand reeds, and the breadth shall be ten thousand: it shall be holy in all its border all around. Of this there shall be a five hundred by five hundred square for the holy place; and fifty cubits for its suburbs all around. Of this measure you shall measure a length of […]
echoes.note: The square 'holy portion' set apart with the sanctuary in it — undergirds the foursquare, sanctified dimensions of the city (v.16).

echoes.text: and the cups, and the snuffers, and the basins, and the spoons, and the fire pans, of pure gold; and the hinges, both for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the house, of the temple, of gold.
echoes.note: The temple's pure gold furnishings — contributes to the 'pure gold, like pure glass' city/street imagery (v.18,21).

echoes.text: For Jerusalem will be built with sapphires, emeralds, and precious stones; your walls and towers and battlements with pure gold. The streets of Jerusalem will be paved with beryl, carbuncle, and stones of Ophir.
echoes.note: Second-Temple parallel: New Jerusalem 'built with sapphires and emeralds... your walls and towers and battlements with pure gold... the streets of Jerusalem with beryl and ruby and stones of Ophir' — strikingly close to v.18-21 (gold, gems, jeweled streets). Likely shared exegetical tradition on Isa 54.

echoes.text: For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron. I will also make your officers peace, and righteousness your ruler.
echoes.note: 'For bronze I will bring gold' — the eschatological upgrade of building materials feeds the all-gold city (v.18,21).

echoes.text: They set in it four rows of stones. A row of ruby, topaz, and beryl was the first row; and the second row, a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald; and the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; and the fourth row, a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. They were enclosed in gold settings. The stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his […]
echoes.note: The made breastpiece stones (parallel list to Exod 28) — secondary attestation of the twelve-stone priestly source for v.19-20.

pericopes.text: I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God, the Almighty, and the Lamb, are its temple. The city has no need for the sun, neither of the moon, to shine, for the very glory of God illuminated it, and its lamp is the Lamb. The nations will walk in its light. The kings of the earth bring the glory and honor of the nations into it. Its gates will in no way be shut by day (for there will be no night there), and they shall bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it so that they may enter. There will in no way enter into it anything profane, or one who causes an abomination or a lie, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s book of life.

echoes.text: The sun shall be no more your light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light to you: but Yahweh will be to you an everlasting light, and your God your glory. Your sun shall no more go down, neither shall your moon withdraw itself; for Yahweh will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning shall be ended.
echoes.note: 'The sun shall be no more your light by day... but the LORD will be your everlasting light' — direct source for 'the city has no need for the sun, neither of the moon... the very glory of God illuminated it' (v.23). Highest verbal and thematic correspondence in the pericope.

echoes.text: Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.
echoes.note: 'Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising' underlies 'the nations will walk in its light. The kings of the earth bring...' (v.24). Isa 60 is the controlling text for v.23-26.

echoes.text: Your gates also shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring to you the wealth of the nations, and their kings led captive.
echoes.note: 'Your gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day or night, that men may bring to you the wealth of the nations' — direct source for 'its gates will in no way be shut' and the bringing-in of the nations' glory (v.25-26).

echoes.text: Then you shall see and be radiant, and your heart shall thrill and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be turned to you, the wealth of the nations shall come to you.
echoes.note: 'The wealth/abundance of the nations shall come to you' — supports 'the glory and honor of the nations' brought into the city (v.24,26).

echoes.text: It shall be eighteen thousand reeds around: and the name of the city from that day shall be, Yahweh is there.
echoes.note: The city's name 'The LORD is there' (YHWH-shammah) — God's unmediated presence stands behind 'no temple... for the Lord God... and the Lamb are its temple' (v.22).

echoes.text: It will be a unique day which is known to Yahweh; not day, and not night; but it will come to pass, that at evening time there will be light.
echoes.note: 'A unique day... not day and not night, but at evening time there shall be light' — source for the perpetual-light / 'no night there' motif (v.23,25). Cf. Zech 14:6 (no cold/frost) and 14:8 (living waters).

echoes.text: Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion; put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean.
echoes.note: 'There shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean' underlies 'there will in no way enter into it anything profane' (v.27); the holy city's purity-boundary.

echoes.text: Thus says the Lord Yahweh, No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any foreigners who are among the children of Israel.
echoes.note: 'No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart or flesh, shall enter my sanctuary' — purity-exclusion source for v.27; pairs with Isa 52:1.

echoes.text: A highway will be there, a road, and it will be called The Holy Way. The unclean shall not pass over it, but it will be for those who walk in the Way. Wicked fools will not go there.
echoes.note: The Holy Way on which 'the unclean shall not pass over it' — supports the exclusion of the profane/unclean (v.27).

echoes.text: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, and not be written with the righteous.
echoes.note: 'Let them be blotted out of the book of the living' — the negative counterpart behind 'only those who are written in the Lamb's book of life' (v.27). Cf. Exod 32:32-33; Dan 12:1.

echoes.text: Men will dwell therein, and there will be no more curse; but Jerusalem will dwell safely.
echoes.note: 'Jerusalem shall dwell in security, there shall be no more curse/ban' — supports the secure, unbarred-gates and no-defilement picture (v.25,27); fully echoed at Rev 22:3.

echoes.text: He will destroy in this mountain the surface of the covering that covers all peoples, and the veil that is spread over all nations. He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.
echoes.note: The destruction of the covering/veil over the nations on the mountain — undergirds the unmediated divine presence ('no temple,' v.22) and the nations' inclusion.

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
echoes.note: 'Everyone whose name shall be found written in the book' shall be delivered — parallel to the Lamb's book of life (v.27); also undergirds Rev 13:8; 20:15.

echoes.text: and I will shake all nations. The precious things of all nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory, says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: 'The treasures/desire of all nations shall come, and I will fill this house with glory' — possible coloring of the nations bringing their glory into the temple-city (v.24,26).

echoes.text: The kings of Tarshish and of the islands will bring tribute. The kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts. Yes, all kings shall fall down before him. All nations shall serve him.
echoes.note: Kings bringing tribute and all nations serving — royal-homage background to 'the kings of the earth bring the glory and honor of the nations' (v.24).

pericopes.text: He showed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb, in the middle of its street. On this side of the river and on that was the tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruits, yielding its fruit every month. The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. There will be no curse any more. The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants serve him. They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads. There will be no night, and they need no lamp light; for the Lord God will illuminate them. They will reign forever and ever.

echoes.text: He brought me back to the door of the house; and behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward; (for the forefront of the house was toward the east;) and the waters came down from under, from the right side of the house, on the south of the altar. Then he brought me out by the way of the gate northward, and led me round by the way outside to the outer gate, by the way of the gate that looks toward the east; and behold, there ran […]
echoes.note: The temple-river flowing out from under the threshold, with fruit trees on both banks bearing fresh fruit monthly and leaves for healing, is the dominant structural model for the river + tree(s) + monthly fruit + healing-leaves cluster. Volume and recurrence both very strong (Hays). LXX and Hebrew agree closely on the healing-leaves motif (Ezek 47:12).

echoes.text: Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers.
echoes.note: The tree of life in Eden's midst and the river going out of Eden to water the garden. Eschaton-as-restored-Eden; thematic coherence and recurrence with Gen 3 are decisive. 'In the middle of its street' echoes the tree 'in the middle of the garden' (Gen 2:9).

echoes.text: Yahweh God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...” Therefore Yahweh God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken. So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim/f + cherubim are powerful angelic creatures, messengers of God with wings. See Ezekiel 10./f* at the east of the garden of […]
echoes.note: Reversal of the expulsion: access to the tree of life, barred by the cherubim and flaming sword, is now restored to the servants (cf. 22:14). The 'no more curse' note ties directly back to the Eden judgment. Strong figural reversal.

echoes.text: It will happen in that day, that living waters will go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea; in summer and in winter will it be.
echoes.note: Living waters going out from Jerusalem feeds the 'water of life' image; Zech 14 is a recurring matrix for Rev 21–22 (see also 14:7, 14:11). Coherence with Ezekiel's temple-river tradition.

echoes.text: Men will dwell therein, and there will be no more curse; but Jerusalem will dwell safely.
echoes.note: 'There shall be no more curse/utter destruction (cherem); Jerusalem shall dwell securely.' Direct verbal-thematic source for 'There will be no curse any more.' Hebrew cherem (devoted-to-destruction); LXX renders anathema — Rev's katathema is closer to the LXX register.

echoes.text: The sun shall be no more your light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light to you: but Yahweh will be to you an everlasting light, and your God your glory.
echoes.note: No sun or moon for light, for the LORD will be everlasting light. Direct source for 'no night... no lamp... the Lord God will illuminate them.' Coherence with Rev 21:23. LXX and Hebrew agree.

echoes.text: But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.
echoes.note: The saints of the Most High receive and possess the kingdom; ground of 'they will reign forever and ever.' Coherence with Rev 5:10, 20:4. Aramaic/OG both attest eternal reign of the holy ones.

echoes.text: The kingdom and the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole sky, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High: his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.
echoes.note: The kingdom and dominion given to the people of the saints of the Most High, an everlasting kingdom — reinforces the reign motif. Closely paired with 7:18.

echoes.text: Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’ “So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.”
echoes.note: Aaronic blessing: the LORD make his face shine upon you, and his name put upon the people of Israel. Strong conceptual pairing for 'see his face' + 'his name on their foreheads.' The name-bestowal of v.27 is the key link; coherence with Rev 3:12, 14:1.

echoes.text: As for me, I shall see your face in righteousness. I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with seeing your form.
echoes.note: 'I shall behold your face in righteousness; I shall be satisfied when I awake with your likeness.' Beatific-vision source for 'They will see his face.' LXX Ps 16:15.

echoes.text: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When shall I come and appear before God?
echoes.note: 'When shall I come and appear before God / see the face of God?' Thirst-for-the-vision motif; fainter, conceptual. LXX Ps 41:3 reads 'see the face of God' where MT has 'appear before.' Flag LXX vs Hebrew divergence.

echoes.text: It will be a unique day which is known to Yahweh; not day, and not night; but it will come to pass, that at evening time there will be light.
echoes.note: A unique day, not day and not night, but at evening time there shall be light. Underlies 'no night... the Lord God will illuminate them' alongside Isa 60:19. Coherence within the Zech 14 matrix.

echoes.text: There is a river, the streams of which make the city of God glad, the holy place of the tents of the Most High.
echoes.note: 'A river whose streams make glad the city of God.' River-in-the-city image feeds the throne-river flowing through the street; thematic coherence. LXX Ps 45:5.

echoes.text: It shall be eighteen thousand reeds around: and the name of the city from that day shall be, Yahweh is there.
echoes.note: 'The LORD is there' (YHWH-shammah) as the city's name; faint support for the divine presence/illumination and name-bearing themes climaxing the new Jerusalem.

echoes.text: It will happen in that day, that the mountains will drop down sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, all the brooks of Judah will flow with waters, and a fountain will flow out from Yahweh’s house, and will water the valley of Shittim.
echoes.note: A fountain coming forth from the house of the LORD, watering the valley — a parallel temple-river tradition reinforcing Ezek 47 / Zech 14. Faint, contested as direct source.
