echoes.text: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.
echoes.note: 'He will swallow up death forever' — broader curse-removal / no-more-tears matrix behind 'no more curse'; faint here, stronger at Rev 21:4.

pericopes.text: He said to me, “These words are faithful and true. The Lord God of the spirits of the prophets sent his angel to show to his bondservants the things which must happen soon.” “Behold, I come quickly. Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.” Now I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. When I heard and saw, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who had shown me these things. He said to me, “See you don’t do it! I am a fellow bondservant with you and with your brothers, the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.”

echoes.text: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these:
echoes.note: 'There is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known... what will be in the latter days / what must happen.' Source for the apocalyptic formula 'the things which must happen soon' (with Dan 2:29, 2:45). Rev 1:1 and 22:6 frame the book by this Danielic idiom.

echoes.text: They fell on their faces, and said, “God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and will you be angry with all the congregation?”
echoes.note: 'O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh.' Title source for 'the Lord God of the spirits of the prophets' (Rev adapts 'of all flesh' to 'of the prophets'). Coherence with Num 27:16.

echoes.text: “Let Yahweh, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,
echoes.note: 'Let the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation.' Parallel divine title behind 'the God of the spirits of the prophets.' Paired with Num 16:22.

echoes.text: Behold, the Lord Yahweh will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
echoes.note: 'Behold, the Lord GOD comes... his reward is with him.' The coming-with-recompense formula introduced here ('Behold, I come quickly') is fully developed in 22:12; Isa 40:10 is its base text. LXX and Hebrew agree on misthos/reward.

echoes.text: The vision of the evenings and mornings which has been told is true: but seal up the vision; for it belongs to many days to come.
echoes.note: 'Seal up the vision, for it pertains to many days hence' — inverted at Rev 22:10 ('don't seal') and resonant with 'the time is at hand'; here the 'faithful and true / soon' framing sets up that contrast. Faint at this pericope.

echoes.text: So he came near where I stood; and when he came, I was frightened, and fell on my face: but he said to me, Understand, son of man; for the vision belongs to the time of the end.
echoes.note: Daniel falls before the angelic interpreter (cf. 10:9). Background for John falling to worship the revealing angel, though the prohibition of angel-worship is distinctive to Rev. Faint, generic.

pericopes.text: He said to me, “Don’t seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is at hand. He who acts unjustly, let him act unjustly still. He who is filthy, let him be filthy still. He who is righteous, let him do righteousness still. He who is holy, let him be holy still.” “Behold, I come quickly. My reward is with me, to repay to each man according to his work. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.

echoes.text: Many shall purify themselves, and make themselves white, and be refined; but the wicked shall do wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand; but those who are wise shall understand.
echoes.note: 'Many shall purify themselves... but the wicked shall act wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand, but the wise shall understand.' Direct source for the let-the-unjust-remain-unjust / let-the-righteous-remain-righteous antithesis. Strong volume and verbal echo (esp. OG/Theodotion).

echoes.text: But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run back and forth, and knowledge shall be increased.”
echoes.note: 'Shut up the words, and seal the book, until the time of the end' — pointedly REVERSED by 'Don't seal up the words... for the time is at hand.' Programmatic inversion (with Dan 12:9). Hays: recurrence + thematic coherence high.

echoes.text: This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.
echoes.note: 'I am the first and I am the last; besides me there is no god.' Direct source for 'the First and the Last' (and the Alpha–Omega equivalent). Near-quotation of a divine self-identification applied to the risen Lord. LXX and Hebrew agree.

echoes.text: “Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.
echoes.note: 'I am he; I am the first, and I am the last.' Second base text for 'the First and the Last.' Paired with Isa 44:6; coherence with Rev 1:17, 21:6.

echoes.text: Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, Yahweh, the first, and with the last, I am he.”
echoes.note: 'I, the LORD, the first, and with the last, I am he' — third witness to the first/last self-predication, calling the generations from the beginning. Reinforces 22:13.

echoes.text: If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this”; doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not render to every man according to his work?
echoes.note: 'Will he not repay each according to his work?' Direct source for 'to repay to each man according to his work.' Strong verbal correspondence (kata ta erga). LXX agrees.

echoes.text: Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.
echoes.note: 'You repay each according to his work.' Parallel source for the recompense-by-works formula (Ps 61:13 LXX). Often cited jointly with Prov 24:12 in NT (cf. Rom 2:6).

echoes.text: Behold, the Lord Yahweh will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
echoes.note: 'Behold, the Lord GOD comes... his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.' Direct source for 'My reward is with me.' LXX and Hebrew agree (misthos).

echoes.text: Behold, Yahweh has proclaimed to the end of the earth, “Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Behold, your salvation comes. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.’”
echoes.note: 'Behold, your salvation comes; behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.' Twin to Isa 40:10 behind 'My reward is with me, to repay each.' Coherence strong.

echoes.text: I, Yahweh, search the mind, I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.
echoes.note: 'I the LORD search the heart... to give to each according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds.' Reinforces recompense-by-works; thematic, slightly fainter than Prov/Ps.

echoes.text: Give them according to their work, and according to the wickedness of their doings. Give them according to the operation of their hands. Bring back on them what they deserve.
echoes.note: 'Repay them according to their work / the work of their hands.' Another recompense-by-deeds source (Ps 27:4 LXX); conceptual, paired with Prov 24:12.

echoes.text: He said, Go your way, Daniel; for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.
echoes.note: 'The words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.' Restates 12:4; sharpens the reversal at Rev 22:10. Coherence within the Daniel-sealing motif.

echoes.text: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
echoes.note: 'The vision is yet for the appointed time... it will surely come, it will not delay' — supports 'the time is at hand' / 'I come quickly.' Faint, conceptual.

echoes.text: Wail; for the day of Yahweh is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty.
echoes.note: 'The day of the LORD is at hand' — generic 'time/day is near' idiom behind 'the time is at hand.' Common prophetic formula, not a single source.

pericopes.text: Blessed are those who do his commandments,that they may have the right to the tree of life, and may enter in by the gates into the city. Outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood. I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you for the assemblies. I am the root and the offspring of David; the Bright and Morning Star.” The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” He who hears, let him say, “Come!” He who is thirsty, let him come. He who desires, let him take the water of life freely.

echoes.text: Yahweh God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...” Therefore Yahweh God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken. So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim/f + cherubim are powerful angelic creatures, messengers of God with wings. See Ezekiel 10./f* at the east of the garden of […]
echoes.note: Right to the tree of life and entry restored — direct reversal of the barred access after Eden's expulsion. Coherence with 22:2; the 'right to the tree of life' is the Edenic inheritance regranted.

echoes.text: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.
echoes.note: 'A shoot from the stump of Jesse, a branch from his roots.' Source for 'the root... of David.' Davidic-messianic root imagery; coherence with Rev 5:5. LXX 'rhiza' matches 'root.'

echoes.text: It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.
echoes.note: 'The root of Jesse, who shall stand as a signal to the peoples; him shall the nations seek.' Direct source for 'the root... of David' as the messianic ensign; LXX explicit 'rhiza tou Iessai.'

echoes.text: I see him, but not now. I see him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob. A scepter will rise out of Israel, and shall strike through the corners of Moab, and break down all the sons of Sheth.
echoes.note: Balaam: 'a star shall come out of Jacob, a scepter shall rise out of Israel.' Source for 'the Bright and Morning Star' as messianic title. Strong messianic-star tradition (also at Qumran); coherence with Rev 2:28.

echoes.text: “Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
echoes.note: 'Everyone who thirsts, come to the waters... without money and without price.' Direct source for 'He who is thirsty, let him come... take the water of life freely (dorean).' Strong verbal + thematic. LXX dorean matches.

echoes.text: House of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Come, let us walk in the light of the LORD' — invitation-to-come framing; faint background to the threefold 'Come!' Generic invitation idiom.

echoes.text: You shall not bring the hire of a prostitute, or the wages of a male prostitute, into the house of Yahweh your God for any vow; for both of these are an abomination to Yahweh your God.
echoes.note: 'Dogs' excluded from the assembly (the 'wages of a dog' barred from the house of the LORD) — possible background for 'Outside are the dogs.' Conceptual; the metaphor is debated.

echoes.text: Open to me the gates of righteousness. I will enter into them. I will give thanks to Yah. This is the gate of Yahweh; the righteous will enter into it.
echoes.note: 'Open to me the gates of righteousness... this is the gate of the LORD; the righteous shall enter through it.' Faint background for the righteous entering by the gates into the city. Conceptual.

echoes.text: Open the gates, that the righteous nation may enter: the one which keeps faith.
echoes.note: 'Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith may enter in.' Reinforces the gates-entry-of-the-righteous motif behind 'enter in by the gates into the city.' Faint.

pericopes.text: I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book, if anyone adds to them, may God add to him the plagues which are written in this book. If anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, may God take away his part from the tree of life, and out of the holy city, which are written in this book. He who testifies these things says, “Yes, I come quickly.” Amen! Yes, come, Lord Jesus. The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with all the saints. Amen.

echoes.text: You shall not add to the word which I command you, neither shall you take away from it, that you may keep the commandments of Yahweh your God which I command you.
echoes.note: 'You shall not add to the word which I command you, nor take from it.' Direct source for the add/take-away canonical-formula warning. Strong verbal correspondence (prostithemi / aphaireo). LXX and Hebrew agree.

echoes.text: Whatever thing I command you, that you shall observe to do. You shall not add to it, nor take away from it.
echoes.note: 'Whatever I command you... you shall not add to it nor take from it.' (Deut 13:1 in MT/LXX.) Twin to Deut 4:2 behind the don't-add / don't-take-away warning. Coherence high.

echoes.text: Don’t you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.
echoes.note: 'Do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you be found a liar.' Direct source — the 'add to his words' + threatened penalty pattern matches 'if anyone adds... may God add the plagues.' LXX agrees.

echoes.text: “‘If you walk contrary to me, and won’t listen to me, then I will bring seven times more plagues on you according to your sins.
echoes.note: 'I will bring more plagues upon you, sevenfold for your sins' — covenant-curse 'add plagues' formula behind 'may God add to him the plagues.' Coherence with the Exodus-plagues motif in Rev 15–16. LXX plege.

echoes.text: Yahweh will not pardon him, but then Yahweh’s anger and his jealousy will smoke against that man, and all of the curse that is written in this book will fall on him, and Yahweh will blot out his name from under the sky.
echoes.note: 'The LORD will blot out his name... and all the curses written in this book will fall on him.' Background for 'may God take away his part... which are written in this book' (blotting / written-curses). Coherence with the Deuteronomic curse tradition.

echoes.text: Yahweh said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.
echoes.note: 'Whoever has sinned against me, I will blot out of my book.' Faint background for taking away one's 'part from the tree of life' / removal from the book/city (book-of-life motif). Conceptual.

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
echoes.note: Deliverance for those 'found written in the book' — faint support for the inscribed-in/erased-from-the-city-and-life motif behind the take-away penalty. Faint.
